The page uses the rights of the signed-in user and the chart adds no role: without the right to create a Failover it says that the failover-admin role is needed. Experimental.

  • The replication policy page shows how each running VM can be recovered (#44, step 2). The policy status has a new list vms: for each running VM, its disks, the copy moment, the consistency and commonMoments, the moments that all its disks can show (the copy moment and the restore points every disk has), newest first. Only those moments are safe, because disks rewound to different moments would give the guest a mix of two times. The controller works them out from the restore point moments each disk now reports (new restorePointMoments on the disk status, and on the apply and send Job results and the receiver's commit answer). The console policy page has a read-only "Recovery" table: copy moment, consistency, the moments to recover to, and a warning when the newest copy is older than twice the schedule or the disks share no moment. It is the source cluster's view and can be a few minutes old; a Failover plan is exact. The Recovery page with buttons is step 3.

  • A Failover resource plans and carries out a failover on the destination cluster (#44, step 1). The new cluster-scoped Failover (short name fo) has action: Plan or Execute, and optional source, rewindTo, namespace and force. A controller on the leader starts a Job in kube-system that mounts the destination claim and runs the new driver mode --mode=failover. That mode runs the same code as kubectl failover (failover.BuildPlan, which the CLI now calls too), and a test checks that the CLI and the Job give the same plan from the same share. The Job reports in its termination message; the status then lists each VM, the moment it will show, the moments to choose from, which disks must be rewound, the volumes and the RPO. For an Execute the controller also makes the SubVolume, PV and PVC objects. A validating webhook refuses an Execute unless a Plan for the same source and rewindTo finished in the last 15 minutes, and refuses a VM or claim that was failed over on this cluster before. The Job checks the confirmed plan against the share again before it changes anything. New ClusterRole <release>-failover-admin, bound to nobody. The Execute also needs drPool (the CLI's --dr-pool); drShareIP and drExportPath default to the NFS volume behind the claim. Experimental. The console page is the next step.

  • Browse and download files from a backup, part 3 (issue #92). New kubectl backup ls, get and browse for plain volumes in a snapshot pool, at the latest copy or at a moment, through a new backup gateway (a Deployment, a Service and, on OpenShift, a reencrypt Route). The gateway checks the user's own token and, on every call, get backupfiles in the claim's namespace; the built-in admin role has it (the new backup-file-reader is aggregated into it), others need a RoleBinding. Helper calls are over TLS pinned to the session's certificate. Starts, downloads and closes are audit Events with the user and the path. Security change from part 2: helper pods, session Secrets and the NetworkPolicy now live in their own namespace, ibm-vpc-file-pool-csi-browse (value backupBrowse.namespace), which holds nothing else, so the gateway can read Secrets only there; the chart makes the namespace (Pod Security baseline, and one SCC on OpenShift), and the controller copies the image pull secrets into it. Sessions that part 2 left in the release namespace end by themselves. The chart test test/chart/test-browse.sh was changed for the new namespace.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Failover: an Execute on a standard install now works. The controller read the share address only from an NFS volume behind the receiver's data claim, so a claim that the driver provisioned (a CSI volume, as in the tutorials) failed with "not an NFS volume; set spec.drShareIP and spec.drExportPath", and the console never sets those. It now reads the server, share and subDir attributes of a volume of this driver (the same ones the node mounts with); a volume of another driver, or with an unsafe path, is refused. spec.drShareIP and spec.drExportPath still win, and NFS volumes work as before.
  • Failover: a Plan on a claim with no pvcs folder, or none that holds a replicated volume, now fails with a message that says what it looked for and where, and names destinationBasePath. It used to end Planned with no VMs and no error. New optional spec.basePath (the policy's destinationBasePath, default /) makes the Job read <claim>/<basePath>/pvcs, so a policy with destinationBasePath: /repl (Tutorial 12) can be failed over; the Plan names the basePath to use when it finds copies elsewhere. An Execute needs a Plan with the same basePath. The same empty-share check applies to kubectl failover plan.
  • Failover: an Execute now also refuses when a planned volume would go to a different claim, namespace, folder or owner than the confirmed Plan showed. Before, it compared only the VM names, their moments and the volume names, so the share could change where a volume went after the operator confirmed.
  • The design rules in CLAUDE.md now name the one case where a volume request creates a share: auto-expand (issue #222). The code and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md already did this; the rule text said never.
  • Console: the restore and clone banner no longer says "ready" when the claim is Bound but the copy state of its SubVolume has not been read yet (issue #224).
  • PoolBench: when no whole steady phase of the VMs lies inside a backup event, the event says it has no latency figure. Before, it said nothing, so a short backup looked like a missing number.

docs.title: [v0.15.3] — 2026-10-28
docs.text: A small fix release. No CRD changes and no chart value changes.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • PoolBench: the backup event now reports the copy speed (copySpeedAvgMBps, copySpeedMaxMBps). The PoolBench service had no right to read replication policies, so it read no speed and said nothing. The chart role now allows get and list on replication policies, and the service logs an error if the read fails.

docs.title: [v0.15.2] — 2026-10-28
docs.text: A small fix release. No CRD changes and no chart value changes.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • The volume resizer sidecar can watch pods. The controller role allowed only get and list on pods, so the sidecar logged "Failed to watch *v1.Pod" for ever and, on some clusters, restarted without end (161 restarts in a day on one cluster).

docs.title: [v0.15.1] — 2026-10-28
docs.text: A fix release. A COS export of a backup no longer reads a disk that changes under it, and the adaptive copy speed works for VMs with several disks. One additive CRD change (PoolBench status). No chart value changes.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• The adaptive copy speed now changes the speed of a VM copy that has two disks when one disk has finished. Before, the change failed on the finished disk and the disk that still copied kept its first speed (issue #313).
  • A COS export can no longer be torn (issue #310). While the export of a volume runs, the next local backup of that volume waits, so the export does not hold a mix of two moments. Other volumes are not held, but all disks of a running VM are held together (issue #315: before, the other disk was copied alone, from another moment, and the VM could not be copied again); a hold ends with the export or after 6 hours. Restore points of a volume get older by the length of its export.

docs.title: Added
docs.text: • PoolBench: the backup event reports the average and highest copy speed of the running-VM copies (status.events[].copySpeedAvgMBps, copySpeedMaxMBps) and the VMs' p95 latency during the backup against the step before it (p95Micros, p95BeforeMicros). The event message says both.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• The copy of a running VM's disks adapts its speed to the load on the share. The copy of each disk starts at 15 MB/s, speeds up by 5 MB/s every 30 s while the average latency of the share the VM reads (read from the node agents, median of the last three intervals) stays under 15 ms, and halves when it passes that. New spec.vmCopyAdaptive (default true) and spec.vmCopyMaxLatencyMs (1 to 20, default 15) on BackupPolicy and ReplicationPolicy; status.subVolumeStatuses[].vmCopy.speedMBps shows the speed now. The controller reads the node agents' metrics (--node-metrics-service, --node-metrics-ca, a ConfigMap or secret for the CA, a Role to list endpoint slices). It does not send its own token to the node agents: it asks for a one-hour token of a service account <release>-node-reader, which can only read /metrics (--node-metrics-account). The console forms say "highest speed" and show "Adapts to the load on the share". Without them the copy runs at a fixed speed. The reader moved from pkg/poolbench to pkg/nodestats. See docs/specs/2026-10-26-adaptive-copy-speed.md.
  • Snapshot copies of running VM disks adapt their speed too. They follow the same rule as replication and backup: start at 15 MB/s, grow while the share is quiet, halve when it is busy. On the VolumeSnapshotClass, vmCopySpeedLimitMBps is now the highest speed, and the new parameter vmCopyAdaptive: "false" keeps the old fixed speed (default 20 MB/s). Without the node agents' metrics the copy stays fixed.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• The fixed 20 MB/s default copy speed is gone for adaptive copies. spec.vmCopySpeedLimitMBps is now the highest speed of an adaptive copy; unset means no highest speed. With vmCopyAdaptive: false, or when the node agents' metrics cannot be read, it is still the fixed speed (unset means 20, 0 means no limit). Policies that already stored 20 keep it as their highest speed.

  • PoolBench spec.startAfter: a run waits until the named run has ended, so a series of tiers runs one after another. The dp2 size and IOPS table is also written to pkg/ibmcloud/testdata/dp2-ranges.golden.json for the console's new-run form.

  • PoolBench metrics are scraped (a ServiceMonitor, or the user workload monitoring Service whose Endpoints the controller keeps, --monitoring-poolbench-service and --monitoring-poolbench-port), with a certificate for the service's name. New run gauges poolbench_run_vms, poolbench_run_ready_vms and poolbench_run_step.
  • PoolBench: a ValidatingAdmissionPolicy holds the service account to namespaces and pools named poolbench-* and to binding only its run role there.
  • Console: the PoolBench new-run form has an Events section. The person ticks boot storm, patch window, live migration or snapshot, each with its own help, and chooses the step it runs at; the form refuses a VM count that is not a step of the run.
  • Console: the PoolBench run page has an Events card with one row for each event of the run: the step it runs at, whether it waits, runs or is done, its time, and what happened.
  • PoolBench: backup event. The run makes a second small share, backs up 10% of the VMs (at most 10) with a backup policy while they run, and removes the policy and the share at the end. It needs no object storage bucket. The service may make and delete backup policies, limited by the admission policy to poolbench-* names and to one run's namespace and backup pool, with no export; the run role may label disks. The new-run form and the add-event button offer it.
  • Console: the PoolBench graphs mark the start of each event, as they mark each step.
  • Console: a running PoolBench run has an "Add an event to this step" button: pick boot storm, patch window, live migration or snapshot, and it runs once after the current step is measured. The Markdown report lists the events.
  • PoolBench events: after a step is measured, the run enters an Event stage for each event asked for at that VM count (spec.events). The boot storm restarts every VM at once and reports the time until the last VM sends results again; it ends after 30 minutes at the latest and never fails the run. Linux test VMs now run the load as a system service (poolbench-load) so it restarts after a reboot. The patch window makes every VM run only bursts for 10 minutes (the collector's state answer is burst), then waits until every VM is back under the latency limit. The migration event live-migrates 10% of the VMs (at least 1, at most 10) at once and waits until every migration has ended, counting any that failed. The snapshot event takes an OpenShift snapshot of the same share of VMs while they run and waits until every snapshot is ready. The backup event reports "not available in this version" until it is built.
  • Console: compare PoolBench runs side by side (p95 against VMs, one line per run, and the steps in one table).
  • Console: PoolBench raw results download (CSV) and each VM's result lines, through the console proxy.
  • PoolBench raw results: the service serves each run's raw results (raw.csv, and each VM's lines) over HTTPS on port 8444 to the console's plugin proxy (poolbench), only to people who may get the run.
  • Console: PoolBench run controls (pause, resume, hold, measure longer, skip, stop, clean up; the irreversible ones ask first), downloads (step table CSV, Markdown report, print to PDF) and delete run.
  • Console: a PoolBench New run form with presets, live numbers per step, and checks before Run (images, memory with one node down, disks on the share); three tiers make three runs, each starting after the one before.
  • Console: the PoolBench run page has five live graphs (VMs running, IOPS against the share limit, latency against the limit, throughput, slow VMs against the knee threshold) with a mark at each step, and the VM table shows each VM's last IOPS and p95.
  • Console: a PoolBench tab with the list of runs and a run page (live status line, expected end, result sentence, step results table, settings, test VMs, run log).
  • The PoolBench service (--mode=poolbench, Helm poolBench.enabled, off by default): the runner and the collector in one Deployment with leader election, its own service account, cluster rights limited to namespaces, pools and reading nodes, pods and images, and a run role it binds only in each run's namespace. It starts Windows loads through the guest agent and reads the share's counters from the node agents. The Windows start script moved to pkg/poolbench/guest/windows/start.ps1, which the Bash test reads too.
  • The PoolBench runner: it takes a PoolBench through its checks, makes the run's namespace, secrets, pool and VMs step by step, measures each step, finds the knee, and cleans up; pause, hold, measure longer, skip and stop work; a restart of the service goes on from the status. Each test VM waits before a load phase while the run is paused.
  • The PoolBench collector: test VMs send each result to it, and it keeps the results and publishes them as poolbench_vm_* metrics. The Windows load also sends its results to it. The Go code makes the same load and reads results the same way as the Bash test tooling; golden files in pkg/poolbench/testdata tie the two together.
  • The PoolBench resource and its admission checks: the settings and results of a performance test run that the console will start and show. The service that runs it comes in later changes. See docs/specs/2026-10-25-poolbench.md.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• A PoolBench run made before a spec rule was added can finish and be cleaned up. The webhook no longer checks the spec on an update that leaves the spec as it was.
  • The controller can read the node agents' metrics: it registers the EndpointSlice type, without which the adaptive copy speed could never read a latency and stayed at its start speed.

docs.title: [v0.14.3] — 2026-10-24
docs.text: A fix release for the node agent. Volumes of a deleted share no longer stay mounted on nodes, and share metrics are no longer minutes late on a node with dead mounts. No CRD or chart value changes.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Volumes of a deleted share no longer stay mounted on nodes for good. When a pool was deleted soon after its volumes (as the performance test cleanup does), the share was gone before kubelet unmounted the volumes from the node. umount then waited on an NFS server that never answers, kubelet gave up, the late unmount removed the folder, and every repeat failed with "no mount point specified", so kubelet repeated it forever. The node agent now treats a volume that is already unmounted as done, and detaches a mount whose umount has no answer in 30 s. Found on rovslab-dr-eude, where one node held about 25 such mounts; the fix cleaned all of them.
  • Node agent share metrics are no longer minutes late on a node with dead mounts (issue #251). A node can keep staging mounts of deleted shares, and statfs on each one waits 10 s. The node agent asked the mounts one after the other, so on a rovslab node with about 25 such mounts one read took about 4 minutes, not 30 s. A restarted node agent showed no share series for that long, and a new pool's series came late. The node agent now asks up to 8 mounts at once, and does not ask a mount whose statfs failed again for 5 minutes. That mount's NFS counters are still reported.

docs.title: [v0.14.2] — 2026-10-24
docs.text: A fix release. The node agent metrics endpoint works again on nodes that hold one share twice, the driver refuses volumes on a backup policy's snapshot pool, and the console has three fixes. No CRD or chart value changes.

docs.title: Added
docs.text: • Two new tutorials. Part 15, "Make a VM from the Catalog on a Pool" (docs/TUTORIAL-15-VM-FROM-THE-CATALOG.md), and Part 16, "Backups, Clones and Replication Setup in the Console" (docs/TUTORIAL-16-CONSOLE-BACKUPS-CLONES-RECEIVER.md), with three draw.io diagrams. Both were run end to end on rovslab on 24 October 2026.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• A volume can no longer be made on a backup policy's snapshot pool. A policy stops backing up while its snapshot pool holds any volume, and the console offered that pool's storage class for new volumes, clones, restores and migrations. The driver now refuses CreateVolume on such a pool (FailedPrecondition, naming the policy), and the console leaves those pools out of its lists.

  • Console: the clone and restore pages no longer call their own new claim a taken name. After "Clone to new PVC", "Restore to new PVC" or a backup restore started, the form showed "A claim with this name already exists" under the name, because the page counted the claim it had just made.

  • Tutorials 15 and 16 corrected after a run on rovslab (driver v0.14.1, OpenShift 4.21). Part 15: the claim is Pending during the CDI copy, the copy pods are in the catalog images' namespace, the VM pod label is vm.kubevirt.io/name, the console labels of OpenShift 4.21, and a 3000-IOPS example pool. Part 16: the phase shows Unknown for a few seconds, Size shows - for a plain volume (also in BACKUP-RECOVERY.md), and the clone banner now follows the copy.
  • The node agent metrics endpoint no longer answers HTTP 500 when a node holds the same share twice. Kubelet gives each volume its own staging path, so a node can have several staging mounts of one share (and stale ones of deleted pools). The collector reported each one, Prometheus refused the repeated series, and the whole endpoint, with every share metric and the alerts built on them, showed nothing. It now reports one set of series for each share, using the larger counter of its mounts. Found on rovslab-prod-eude while preparing the performance test.
  • Console: the clone banner no longer says "ready" while the copy still runs. A clone's claim is Bound at once, so the banner after "Clone to new PVC" said the volume was ready before the copy had ended. It now follows the SubVolume's copy, shows its progress, and shows a failed copy.
  • Console: a refused "Delete backups" dialog offers "Close". The button read "Close (the Job goes on)" although no Job had started.
  • Documentation corrections. TUTORIAL.md and its diagram list Parts 15 and 16, and USER-GUIDE.md and Part 14 link to them. Part 14 no longer says the console has no backup screens. UPGRADE-GUIDE.md and API-KEY-SETUP.md use the real Deployment, Service and ServiceAccount names. BACKUP-RECOVERY.md says a restored claim stays Pending until the copy ends. KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md says the StorageProfile patch also resets cloneStrategy. ARCHITECTURE.md and VOLUME-CLONING.md say Jobs do the copies, and ARCHITECTURE.md describes auto-expand in CreateVolume correctly. VM-DISK-FORMATS.md no longer says the driver uses VPC share snapshots. CROSS-REGION-DR.md says kubectl failover does the SubVolume, PV and PVC steps. CONSISTENCY-MODEL.md has a cross-file example that matches its text. VOLUME-CLONING.md describes the clone Job, the Clone Worker and crash recovery as the code does, and BACKUP-RECOVERY.md has one group snapshot notice, not two.

docs.title: [v0.14.1] — 2026-10-24
docs.text: A small release. The driver itself is the same as v0.14.0. The console now shows the driver's real VM snapshot mode, and the chart renders one more ConfigMap for it.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• The console shows the driver's real VM snapshot mode, "copy" or "instant" (spec docs/specs/2026-10-24-console-snapshot-mode.md). The box on the Snapshots and Pools pages used to read only the KubeVirt Sidecar gate, so it said "on" while the driver was set to vmSnapshots.method=copy. The chart now renders a ConfigMap ibm-vpc-file-pool-csi-settings (key vmSnapshotMethod) and a Role that lets signed-in users get that one ConfigMap by name. The box says instant only when the driver is set to auto and the gate is on. A driver that does not publish its setting shows "unknown".
  • Teaching page on instant VM snapshots (docs/diagrams/vm-snapshot-chain.html, now page 12): adds switches for vmSnapshots.method and the KubeVirt Sidecar gate, stop, start and move of the VM with the hook, the guest freeze, the fail-safe start, and flatten.
  • Interactive teaching page 11, "What QEMU does" (docs/diagrams/11-what-qemu-does.html): how QEMU copies a running VM disk at one moment, keeps a change list, and why a VM move makes the next copy a full copy.

docs.title: [v0.14.0] — 2026-10-22
docs.text:
This release adds backup to a snapshot pool and to IBM Cloud Object Storage (COS), instant VM snapshots, replication of running VMs, 21 alerts with real share usage and latency, image and controller hardening, and many fixes.

File-level restore from a backup (issue #92) is NOT in this release. Only its first two parts are here (the browse helper image and the BackupBrowse resource); the console and kubectl backup do not offer a file restore yet.

docs.title: Added (latest changes)
docs.text:
• The replication receiver also bounds the memory used when it writes plain files (issue #225). Like the VM disk path (#212), it now syncs every 32 MiB and drops the cached pages while it extracts files, so a plain volume larger than the receiver memory limit no longer fills the container with dirty NFS pages.

  • Docs corrected against the code. One NFS mount per staged volume (not per share per node); a volume request that finds no room can make a share itself when autoExpand is on; the COS export and Key Protect unwrap were proved against real IBM Cloud in stage 18; Key Protect is reached with a service ID's API key held in a Secret; receiver-mode replication uploads the whole folder each cycle (only direct NFS mode uses rsync); a clone's claim is Bound at once and only the pod mount waits; there is no failback command.

  • Known open items, not in this release: auto-expand makes a share inside the volume request (issue #222); the console restore banner (issue #224); file-level restore from a backup (issue #92); failback has no command and is untested.

  • Interactive teaching pages (docs/diagrams/index.html): ten pages with buttons that step through a story, in plain words. This change adds the index and the pages on the two kinds of volume, replication, backup to COS, cloning a VM disk and a pool filling up.

  • The replication receiver survives a VM disk send, and a receiver that is killed mid-send no longer blocks every retry (issues #212, #213). (1) Data written to a file on NFS counts against the container memory limit until it is on the share, and the kernel cannot free it. A VM disk send filled 2 GB of such pages and the receiver (limit 512Mi) was killed. The receiver now forces its data out every 32 MiB when it writes a disk, an undo file or a new disk, and tells the kernel to drop the cached pages. The chart default receiver memory limit is now 1Gi (was 512Mi). (2) A receiver that was killed while it wrote its upload record left a cut-off entry; the next entries were then written out of step and every retry failed with "the upload record file is damaged". The receiver now keeps the entries it can trust, cuts the record file off at the first damaged entry (a cut-off entry or zeros), and the client sends the rest again. If the stored records do not match the copy's digest, the upload is discarded and the next try starts clean. (3) A Job whose pod restarts in place used up its retries without Kubernetes raising the failed count to the limit, so the controller waited for ever: the policy stayed Sending with no error and the Job was never retried. The controller now treats a Job with the Failed condition as failed, shows the reason in the volume status and the policy error, removes the Job, and starts a new copy at the next scheduled cycle.

  • Failover to an earlier restore point works end to end, and the PVs and PVCs it makes bind and mount correctly (issues #209, #210, #211). kubectl failover execute --rewind-to was refused by the SubVolume rule for spec.subPath, which did not allow the .rewind-<epoch> folder; the dry run did not show it. The rule (CRD and webhook) now allows exactly /pvcs/pvc-<uuid>.rewind-<digits> and nothing else. The tool checks every folder against the CRD rule before it makes anything, in a dry run too, and the dry run shows the rewound folder. The PVs it makes now carry the pool's NFS mount options, including sec=sys (before, a VM got Permission denied on disk.img), and the PVCs ask for no StorageClass (before, they took the cluster default and bound to nothing). Apply the new SubVolume CRD (config/crd) before using --rewind-to. The dry run now reads the pool from the cluster to show the mount options, so give it --kubeconfig.

  • Tests pin two replication fixes found in the 22 October two-cluster run (issues #214, #215). Deleting a policy removes the Jobs, PVCs and PVs of its plain-volume copies (direct and receiver mode), and a plain volume's status follows its Job within one pass while a VM disk is also copying. Both were fixed by #161 and #197, which the image used in that run did not yet contain; no driver code changed.

  • Migrating a claim works for a user with only the edit role (issue #196). The copy pod (kubectl migrate execute and the console page "Migrate volumes into a pool") ran apk add rsync at start, which fails for the random user id that OpenShift gives a normal user. It now uses the OpenShift tools image (openshift/tools:latest in the cluster's registry), which already holds rsync, and it follows the restricted rules (no user id set, no extra rights, all capabilities dropped). The copy runs as the namespace's user, so it no longer sets owners or folder times: the new files belong to that user. Because the user is not root, file owners are not kept, and a file or folder with mode 0600 or 0700 that belongs to someone else cannot be read, so it is not copied (the file counts then differ and the migration is reported as failed). See KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md. The release test for the console migrate page no longer grants the anyuid right.

  • Interactive picture of the VM snapshot chain (docs/diagrams/vm-snapshot-chain.html), linked from VM-INSTANT-SNAPSHOTS.md. Open it in a browser to step through snapshots, writes, restores and merges.

  • Deleting the VolumeSnapshot of a failed snapshot no longer leaves a record that blocks the pool (issue #201). When a snapshot failed (for example an instant snapshot of a disk the VM user does not own), the snapshot sidecar had no snapshot ID, so deleting the VolumeSnapshot never reached the driver and the Snapshot record stayed, which kept the pool in SnapshotsExist. The controller now removes a Snapshot record that is not ready, is at least 2 minutes old, is named by the sidecar (<prefix>-<VolumeSnapshot UID>) and has no VolumeSnapshotContent, with the normal delete (Jobs stopped, files merged away, space given back). This also cleans up records left by older versions. Ready snapshots and records made by group snapshots are never touched.

  • Replication receiver TLS stays off by default; the reason is now written down (issue #89). Turning it on needs cert-manager and a trusted CA on the source cluster, so a new default would break working installs. On OpenShift the Route already encrypts traffic into the cluster. See SECURITY.md. All other items of #89 and #90 were already done.

  • README: a table of every use case and its status (included with its maturity, in progress, proposed, not active).

  • Replication and backup status follow the copy Jobs within seconds (issue #192). Before, a policy looked at its Jobs only when its schedule was next due, so sync in progress stayed for the whole schedule (a first backup took about 13 minutes to show LAST BACKUP). Now a policy with a cycle in progress is checked on every poll (30 seconds), the controllers also watch the Jobs in the driver namespace and wake when one finishes, and the backup controller wakes after each replication pass. Pre-sync hooks still run once at the start of a cycle, and the cycle's duration is measured from its start.

  • Release test stage 16: browser tests for draining a share, migrating a claim and cloning a volume (issue #46, items 5 to 7). Each drives the console page with a token that has only the rights of that page, then checks the cluster. Found issue #196 (migrate fails for a user without the root right on OpenShift).

  • Browse helper for single-file restore, part 1 (issue #92). A new image (browse, built by make docker-build-browse) and program (cmd/browse) that read one backup folder read-only: list, stat, read a byte range, or stream a tar, over HTTP with a session token. Links are listed and never followed, names are raw bytes, and a pipe or device is never opened. It ends when idle or at a time limit. Nothing in the driver starts it yet, so users see no change. Lab result: with root, no capabilities and a read-only mount, it reads another user's files with mode 0600 and folders with mode 0700, so the restore Job that copies as root can too. Release test stage 20 (the spec calls it 19; 19 is taken) checks this on a real share.
  • Instant VM snapshot of a disk owned by another user (issue #191). Before, it failed after the snapshot was taken with chmod: changing permissions ... Operation not permitted and left an extra overlay file in the disk chain. Now the driver checks the owner of disk.img first and refuses before changing anything, with a message that names the owner and the fix. The Snapshot is marked Failed with that message. If a step fails after the new overlay file is made, the driver merges the file back and deletes it, so the chain is as it was.

  • Browse sessions for single-file restore, part 2 (issue #92). New cluster-scoped BackupBrowse resource and the backup controller part: a helper pod per open session, with a per-session token and TLS certificate in a Secret, limits (15 minutes idle, 2 hours hard, 5 sessions in the cluster and 2 for each namespace), and clean-up of helpers and Secrets whose session is gone. The helper now serves only over TLS and can read a chosen moment. New chart values backupBrowse.*, a Role for the session Secrets in the release namespace, and a NetworkPolicy. Users cannot start a session yet: the gateway comes in part 3. Every object of a session is named by the resource's UID, so a deleted session that is made again with the same name cannot get the old session's Secret or pod.

  • Browse helper for single-file restore, part 1 (issue #92). A new image (browse, built by make docker-build-browse) and program (cmd/browse) that read one backup folder read-only: list, stat, read a byte range, or stream a tar, over HTTP with a session token. Links are listed and never followed, names are raw bytes, and a pipe or device is never opened. It ends when idle or at a time limit. Nothing in the driver starts it yet, so users see no change. Lab result: with root, no capabilities and a read-only mount, it reads another user's files with mode 0600 and folders with mode 0700, so the restore Job that copies as root can too. Release test stage 20 (the spec calls it 19; 19 is taken) checks this on a real share.

  • Console: the restore page no longer spins forever without the right to read VolumeSnapshotContents (issue #186). It now says which right is missing.

  • Console: the delete backups dialog gives an administrator the safe command. When the user lacks the rights, the dialog now shows kubectl backup delete --policy <policy> --pvc <namespace>/<name>, which measures first and asks for the typed claim name. Before, it showed raw YAML that removed the backups with neither step.

  • The documents moved into docs/ (issue #116, part 1). README, CHANGELOG, CONTRIBUTING, CLAUDE.md and SKILL.md stay in the root; every other guide is now in docs/, and the research notes are in docs/archive/. All links, the console's help links, the docs site and the code comments point to the new places. A branch that still edits a guide at its old place: after git merge origin/main stops, run hack/follow-docs-move.sh to carry the edits over.

  • Receiver check on the policy: ReceiverReachable (issue #46, item 4). For a policy in driver-to-driver mode, the replication controller now checks the receiver (it answers, the certificate is trusted, the token is accepted) when it first sees the policy and then once per schedule, and sets the ReceiverReachable condition on status.conditions with a plain reason such as "certificate not trusted" or "token refused". The Replication Policies list has a Receiver column with help text, and the policy page a Receiver Status line. A failing check does not stop replication. The controller reads the two Secrets in kube-system with the rights it already has.

  • Console: the VM warnings on the restore and clone pages are correct again. The restore page no longer says a snapshot of a running VM may not boot; it says the disk was copied at one moment, and what a crash consistent copy means. The clone page points to a VM snapshot for a safe copy.

  • Console says when Red Hat does not support a VM copy. The replication policy pages (when the policy holds a running VM's disk) and the Snapshots page now say that copies and snapshots of running VMs work directly with QEMU, not through OpenShift, so an OpenShift update could stop them until the driver is updated. The Snapshots page adds that instant snapshots also need a KubeVirt setting Red Hat does not support.

  • Sidecar gate Job has fewer rights (issue #154). The hook Job that vmSnapshots.enableSidecarGate runs may now only get and update the HyperConverged object named kubevirt-hyperconverged in openshift-cnv; before, it could list and update every HyperConverged. SECURITY.md now says what the gate opens up.

docs.title: Security
docs.text: • Image hardening (issue #90). The driver image now runs as user 65532 (USER in the Dockerfile). The chart sets security contexts: the controller is non-root with no privilege escalation, all capabilities dropped and the RuntimeDefault seccomp profile; its sidecars get no escalation and no capabilities; the console plugin and replication receiver get the same limits. The node agent explicitly stays root and privileged (it mounts NFS), and Jobs the controller creates keep the users they already set. All of it can be overridden with controller.securityContext, controller.podSecurityContext, controller.sidecarSecurityContext, node.securityContext, replicationReceiver.securityContext and consolePlugin.securityContext. Not lab tested. Off OpenShift the chart adds fsGroup: 65532 to the controller so it can read the webhook key.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • The default image tag is v plus the chart appVersion, not latest (issue #90). image.tag and consolePlugin.image.tag are empty by default. make deploy-style installs that set --set image.tag=... are unchanged. The chart appVersion must be set at release (it is 0.1.0 until then), so an install without image.tag before a release asks for an image that does not exist.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• kubectl backup cos-list failed with an unknown-type error (PR #183). The command's client did not know apps/v1; it does now.
  • A VM disk copy no longer sticks for good when its finished apply Job expires before the controller reads it (issue #160). The apply step now treats a missing staging file as done when the far-site disk already shows that copy, so the Job the controller makes again succeeds. The volume shows "apply Job was gone before its result was read; running it again" meanwhile. Deleting a replication policy now also removes its temporary Jobs, PVCs and PVs in kube-system. Tested with fakes and temporary folders; not lab tested.
  • kubectl backup delete, found by the lab test of issue #124: a shell whose input is /dev/null (a script, CI) counted as interactive, so the command measured the backup and then asked a question nobody could answer, instead of stopping at once as documented; and the size it showed counted every hard-linked file twice for plain volumes. The size is now one du run over both folders. BACKUP-RECOVERY.md lists every right the command needs.
  • Dashboard numbers that did not match their labels. The Allocation Rate cards (dashboard and pool page) showed new volumes per second under a "/hr" label; they now show per hour. The Snapshots card counted every snapshot operation, including deletes and failures; it now counts snapshots taken. The Clones card counted failed clones too, and labelled the median clone time "Avg duration"; it now counts finished clones and says "Median duration".
  • kubectl backup cos-setup could never finish a first run, and lost the HMAC secret (issue #138). IBM Cloud adds an instance-wide Writer policy to the service ID when the HMAC key is made; the safety check then stopped the command before the key file was written. Now the key file is written the moment the key is made, the command deletes that one implicit policy (found by comparing the service ID's policies before and after; it says so in the steps) and then runs the check, which still refuses any other wide policy. A rerun with an HMAC key that exists makes no second key and says its secret cannot be shown again (delete the key to get a new one). A key file with no HMAC key stops the command before a key is made. Found in the first live run; tested with fakes, not rerun on IBM Cloud.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Set up the COS export from the console (issue #46, item 9, step 7). A guide in the COS tab of a policy shows the kubectl backup cos-setup command with your names filled in and what each flag means, then makes the Secrets from the manifests the command wrote (and the Key Protect API key Secret), writes the pasted spec.export block into the policy after the webhook's checks, and says whether the export works. The console still does not run cos-setup (no IBM Cloud login in a browser, and no IBM Cloud API key in the console); this is the one part of the backup tools it cannot match. It never reads a Secret back, refuses Secrets outside the driver namespace or with unknown keys, and refuses the readable backup key.
  • COS tab and restore from COS in the console (issue #46, item 9, step 6). A COS tab on a backup policy page shows the export settings (Secret names only) and the export state of each volume, and List COS contents runs the read-only list Job (built by the same code as the Go one, golden file) and shows volumes and moments. A Restore from COS page makes a BackupRestore with spec.fromCOS: fill the settings from a policy or type them for another cluster's bucket, pick a volume and moment from the list, and give the namespace, name, storage class and size. The console does not remove delete markers and does not fetch the wrapped key from the bucket (no IBM Cloud login); the page says so. Not run on a real bucket.
  • Controller metrics are secured, and alerts work on OpenShift in a supported way (issue #117). The controller's :8080/metrics is now HTTPS with a token login and a certificate Prometheus checks (from webhook.certProvider); anything that scraped it over plain HTTP must change. On OpenShift (metrics.monitoring.mode: auto) the chart makes the namespace ibm-vpc-file-pool-csi-monitoring for the ServiceMonitor objects, the PrometheusRule and two selector-less Services whose Endpoints the controller keeps, because platform monitoring does not read kube-system and Red Hat does not support labelling it. OpenShift's user workload monitoring must be on (enableUserWorkload: true), or no alert fires; the chart does not change that setting, and the controller warns at start if it is off. See MONITORING.md, "Where alerts run on OpenShift". The controller role gets token and access review rights.
  • Delete the backups of a volume in the console (issue #46, item 9, step 5). A Delete backups action on each volume of a backup policy opens a dialog that does the steps of kubectl backup delete: it refuses while the policy still backs up the volume or a restore of it has not ended (in the words of the command), starts the measure Job and shows the size and the number of moments, asks you to type namespace/name, then starts the delete Job and follows it. The Jobs are built by the same code as the Go ones (golden file, step 4) and removed when they end. Without the rights, the dialog names them and shows the YAML for an administrator. ?claim=<namespace>/<name> on the policy page opens the dialog, so the file-restore page (issue #92) can link to it. Not run on a real cluster yet: the release-test browser stage is still to do.

  • Console builders for the backup Jobs, tied to Go by a golden file (issue #46, item 9, step 4). A Go test (pkg/pool/share_job_backup_golden_test.go) writes the PV, claim and Job that the driver makes to measure and to remove the backup of one volume, and the Job that lists a COS bucket, to pkg/pool/testdata/backup-jobs.golden.json. The console builders (console-plugin/src/utils/backup-jobs.ts) build the same objects from the same input and a console test compares them, so the two cannot drift apart. No change to the driver. The delete dialog and the COS tab use these builders in the next steps.

  • Real used bytes and NFS latency and IOPS for each share, with alerts (issue #117). The node agent now serves metrics on port 9810 (node.metricsPort) over HTTPS; a caller needs a token that may get /metrics, and the chart binds a new metrics-reader role to prometheus-k8s. The endpoint serves a certificate that Prometheus checks (from webhook.certProvider: OpenShift service CA, cert-manager, or your own secret), so the scrape token cannot be given to a stranger. It reads statfs and /proc/self/mountstats of each staged share every 30 s, so nothing walks the files. New metrics: vpc_file_pool_share_used_bytes, _size_bytes, _nfs_operations_total, _nfs_rtt_seconds_total, _nfs_execute_seconds_total and _nfs_bytes_total. New alerts: VPCFilePoolShareUsedHigh (85%), VPCFilePoolShareUsedCritical (95%), VPCFilePoolShareNFSLatencyHigh (0.1 s, judged only above 1 request a second) and VPCFilePoolShareIOPSHigh (off until metrics.alerts.shareIOPSWarning is set). The node role may now read FileSharePools and create token and access reviews; the node agent adds the dependency k8s.io/apiserver (needed by controller-runtime's metrics login filter). The controller's own :8080/metrics is still plain HTTP without a login.

  • Create, edit, suspend and delete a backup policy in the console (issue #46, item 9, step 3). A form makes or changes a BackupPolicy: snapshot pool (only pools with no workload claims and a ready share can be chosen, the others are shown with the reason), schedule, keep time, labels with a live count of the claims they match, namespaces, VM copy speed limit, and suspend. It explains the stop at 85% full, shows the admission webhook's message when it refuses, and keeps the export block and match expressions of a policy it edits. Suspend, Resume and Delete are on the list and the policy page; the delete dialog says that the backups already made stay on the snapshot pool. Without the right, an action is off and names the missing right.
  • Restore a backup in the console (issue #46, item 9, step 2). A Restore action on each volume of a backup policy opens a page: choose the volume (a volume that is gone is listed too), the latest backup or a time, the namespace, a new claim name (checked live; a name that exists is refused) and a storage class. A confirmation says that a new claim is made, nothing is overwritten and the copy takes time. The console makes one BackupRestore, as kubectl backup restore does, and a banner follows its phase and the restored moment. Without the right to make BackupRestore objects the button is off, the missing right is named, and the YAML for an administrator is shown. The page takes ?claim= and ?moment= so other pages can link to it.
  • Backups tab in the console, read-only (issue #46, item 9, step 1). The Backups tab lists the backup policies, and a policy page shows its settings and each backed-up volume: newest and oldest backup, restore points, size, consistency, error and export state. A volume that is no longer backed up says until when its backups are kept. A banner explains in plain words when backups are stopped because the snapshot pool is more than 85% full, with a link to the pool. Help buttons explain the status columns and cards. The "Browse files" action is built but hidden until the file-restore feature (issue #92) is present. Spec: docs/specs/2026-10-22-console-backup-ui.md.
  • Help on the status columns of the list pages (issue #114, part 2). The Phase, Ready, Clone Status, Last Sync and Failures columns of the Pools, SubVolumes, Snapshots and Replication pages, and the per-volume replication columns, have a help button that says what each value means and what to do. The texts are in console-plugin/src/utils/column-help.ts. The dashboard help for Consecutive Failures now says that a policy pauses at its retry limit.
  • Alert for one nearly full share, and firing alerts on the console dashboard (issue #117). New gauges vpc_file_pool_share_total_gb and vpc_file_pool_share_allocated_gb (labels pool, share), dropped when a share or pool goes away (31 metrics). New alert VPCFilePoolShareNearlyFull (17 alerts; metrics.alerts.shareUtilizationWarning, default 90), tested with promtool. The console dashboard has a "Firing Alerts" card that reads ALERTS from the cluster Prometheus and says when that Prometheus has not loaded the driver's rules. Not done: per-share NFS latency and IOPS, and real used space per share, because the driver has no such data (the node agent has no counters); see MONITORING.md.
  • Help icons on the dashboard and monitoring cards (issue #114). Every number card and chart has a help button that says in one to three plain sentences what the number means, what is normal and what to do when it is bad. The texts are in one file, console-plugin/src/utils/card-help.ts.
  • Help and support (#151). New SUPPORT.md (where to start, common problems, how to get support), scripts/collect-diagnostics.sh (one script for support cases: it reads no Secret and removes key-like values; the old inline scripts in the docs used wrong names), and troubleshooting sections for backups stopped at 85%, a volume with no recent backup, and late or failing replication. The console has a Help link on every page, a "Get help" card on the Overview, and troubleshooting links on the restore-failed, monitoring and loading-error banners. All console links are in console-plugin/src/utils/help-links.ts; test/chart/test-doc-links.sh checks that each linked file and heading exists.
  • The console shows whether instant VM snapshots are on (issue #108). The Pools and Snapshots pages have a status box: "on" (the KubeVirt Sidecar feature gate is on) with the VMs whose disks have instant snapshots, which would not start if the gate were turned off; "off" (snapshots are full copies) with how an administrator turns it on and that Red Hat does not support it; or "unknown" when the user may not read KubeVirt. The console only shows the setting; it has no switch.
  • Helm value vmSnapshots.enableSidecarGate turns on the KubeVirt Sidecar feature gate for instant VM snapshots (issue #107). Off by default. When on, a post-install and post-upgrade hook Job (driver image, new mode enable-sidecar-gate) adds the gate entry to the HyperConverged kubevirt.kubevirt.io/jsonpatch annotation, keeps the other entries, and never adds it twice. An annotation that is not valid JSON is left alone and the Job fails. Uninstalling or setting the value to false does not remove the gate, because VMs with instant snapshots cannot start without it. The Job has its own service account; the install notes say the gate is on and that Red Hat does not support it. The value needs vmSnapshots.method=auto.
  • The chart ships alerts, on by default (21 by this release: capacity, over-committed pools, share limit, allocation failures and slowness, VPC API errors, snapshot failures, replication, backup lateness, COS export lateness, snapshot pool full), with limits under metrics.alerts. Tested with promtool in make test-scripts. New gauge vpc_file_pool_max_shares. The old "at max shares" alert compared a value with itself; it now compares the share count with the limit (#117).
  • Release test stage 18: fast COS mode. COS_QUICK=1 RT_STAGES=18 bash test/release/remote.sh start CLUSTER TAG skips the local restore checks, uses a 1 minute schedule, 1 hour local keep time and a 1 GB data disk, and runs the COS checks only. Not yet run on a cluster.
  • Release test stage 18, COS part: the cos-list check wanted two exports of every volume (fix). The first real run exported to the bucket correctly, but a pod volume that does not change is exported once (the export holds its earlier moment as an undo file), so "two moments" never showed and the wait ended after an hour with the restore checks not run. The check now needs one export per volume, waits at most 30 minutes, prints the kubectl backup cos-list output and exit status on failure, and the restore checks still run.
  • COS export, part 6: release test stage 18, second part (written, not run on a cluster, a bucket or Key Protect). test/e2e/test-backup.sh now also sets spec.export (Compliance lock, keep time 25h, a prefix that is new for each run), waits for exportedTime and exportedBytes on all three volumes and for two moments of each in kubectl backup cos-list, restores the three volumes with kubectl backup restore --from-cos into a second namespace, boots the VM and checks the checksums, and checks the pod volume's first and changed content. With COS_DR_KUBECONFIG it repeats the restore in the other cluster of the lab pair. It runs when COS_BUCKET is set (environment or ~/.config/pool-csi/cos-stage.env; the HMAC key, Key Protect API key and wrapped key files are read from the same folder and never printed) and is reported as not checked otherwise. A failure prints the export status, the restores and the controller log. Objects locked by Compliance are left in the bucket, and the output says so. Helpers are in test/e2e/lib/backup-cos.sh with tests in test/e2e/lib/test-backup-cos.sh (part of make test-scripts). remote.sh copies the settings and keys for the run only and deletes them (COS_DR_CLUSTER adds the other cluster). The stage time limit is now 180 minutes.
  • The console plugin is on by default, and the chart turns it on in the console (issue #131). consolePlugin.enabled now defaults to true, and the plugin is installed only where the cluster has the OpenShift console. A post-install and post-upgrade hook Job adds the plugin to console.operator.openshift.io/cluster spec.plugins; a pre-delete hook Job removes it, and so does an upgrade with consolePlugin.enabled=false. Other plugins are never removed. The Jobs run the driver image in the new modes register-console-plugin and unregister-console-plugin (flag --console-plugin-name), with a service account that can only get and update that one object. The manual oc patch step is gone from INSTALL.md.
  • COS export, part 5: restore from COS and kubectl backup cos-list (not tested against a real bucket or Key Protect). kubectl backup restore --from-cos makes a new PVC from a backup in a COS bucket, in any cluster that runs the driver: no BackupPolicy and no snapshot pool are needed. A BackupRestore has a new optional block spec.fromCOS (bucket, endpoint, prefix, credentials Secret, volume, sizeGB, wrapped-key Secret and keyProtect, or emergencyKeyOnly with emergencyKeySecret); sourceNamespace and sourceName are required only without it. Three Jobs run on the new volume's share: one restores the export read-only from the Kopia repository into a scratch folder, the restore Job of a local restore copies it into the volume, and one removes the scratch folder. Status has two new fields, fetched and copied. The command removes delete markers in the policy's area with the caller's own IBM Cloud login (markers only, by version), makes the wrapped-key Secret from the bucket if the cluster has none, and with --backup-key-file restores with the readable key and never calls Key Protect (its temporary Secret is removed when the restore ends). kubectl backup cos-list lists the volumes and the export moments in the bucket with a read-only Job. New package pkg/cosrestore (plain net/http, no new dependency). ShareData gains FetchFromCOS and RemoveCOSScratch. The webhook requires storageClassName, a pvc-<uuid> volume and a size with fromCOS.
  • COS export, part 3: key handling (not tested against a real Key Protect instance). The backup key is stored only as a Key Protect-wrapped copy. spec.export has a required keyProtect block (instanceID, region, rootKeyID, apiKeySecret) and an optional emergencyKeySecret; backupKeySecret now holds wrappedKey, not a readable key (the Secret cos-setup writes). Export and maintenance Jobs no longer have KOPIA_PASSWORD: they mount the wrapped key, the API key and the optional emergency key as read-only Secret files and run the driver in a new mode, unwrap-backup-key, which unwraps the key with Key Protect and writes it (mode 0400) to a memory-backed folder; the script hands it to Kopia and deletes the file. If Key Protect is unreachable (no connection, a 5xx or 429) and an emergency key is set, the Job uses it and logs that it did; a refusal from Key Protect (wrong root key, bad API key) never falls back. The controller never reads these Secrets and never calls Key Protect (tests check both). New package pkg/keyprotect (plain net/http, no new dependency; IAM token from the API key, wrap, unwrap). The webhook refuses a block without the four keyProtect fields. cos-setup now prints the keyProtect block and the command for the API key Secret. Tested with a fake Key Protect HTTP server and a Kopia repository in a folder.
  • COS export, part 4: kubectl backup cos-setup (not run against real IBM Cloud yet). Automates TUTORIAL-09-COS-BACKUP-BUCKET.md with the caller's own IBM Cloud login (an IAM token or API key from the environment, or the ibmcloud login; never stored or printed): the COS instance, a bucket with versioning and object lock encrypted by a Key Protect root key you give, the custom role PoolCsiBackupWriter (the action list is in one place, pkg/cossetup/roles.go, and a test checks it against the tutorial and that it leaves out object.delete_version, object.bypass_governance_retention and every bucket.put_* and bucket.delete_*), a service ID and HMAC key limited to the one bucket, a CBR zone and rule, and a backup key wrapped by Key Protect. It reuses what exists by name, never deletes anything, refuses a bucket it did not make unless --existing-bucket, refuses an enforced CBR rule when the caller's own address is not in the zone, supports --dry-run, asks for a typed confirmation (or --yes), and for a keep time above 90 days asks for a second one. It writes the COS key to --key-file (Secret manifest, mode 0600), shows the readable backup key once and waits for a typed confirmation that a copy is saved, then stores only the wrapped copy in the bucket and in --secret-file. It prints the spec.export block. New package pkg/cossetup (plain net/http, no new Go dependency); tested with httptest fakes of every API. The Key Protect wrap is a small client inside pkg/cossetup, to be joined with pkg/keyprotect later.
  • COS export, part 2: the controller, status, metrics and the webhook (needs key handling, part 3, to be usable). A BackupPolicy has an optional spec.export block (bucket, endpoint, prefix, credentialsSecret, backupKeySecret, keepFor default 30d, lock Compliance or None, optional schedule). After a local backup of a volume finishes with a moment newer than the last export, the controller starts an export Job for it (one at a time for each policy) and puts the result in the volume's status: new fields exportedTime, exportedBytes and exportError. A failed export is retried after 5 minutes. An export problem never changes the policy's phase or stops the backups to the snapshot pool. Once a volume is exported, a maintenance Job runs every maintenance interval (a day; an hour for the shortest keep time) to extend locks and now also to delete Kopia snapshots older than keepFor; the export sets a Kopia policy so that Kopia itself never drops snapshots by count. The webhook refuses an export block without bucket, endpoint or Secrets, a lock other than Compliance or None, and a Compliance keepFor below 25 hours; the rule is one helper used by the webhook and the controller. ExportToCOS and MaintainCOSRepo are now in the ShareData interface. New metrics vpc_file_pool_backup_export_oldest_unexported_age_seconds and vpc_file_pool_backup_export_newest_age_seconds with example alerts (ExportLate) in MONITORING.md; the chart alerts are issue #117. Tested with fakes and with a Kopia repository in a folder; not tested against a bucket or on a cluster.
  • COS export, part 1: Kopia in the image and the export Jobs (not used by the controller yet). The driver image now holds the Kopia program (0.23.1, checked by SHA-256 in the Dockerfile; used only by Jobs, not linked into the driver). ShareJobRunner has two new methods, ExportToCOS and MaintainCOSRepo, that are not in the ShareData interface. The export Job mounts the snapshot share read-only, connects to (or creates) the Kopia repository in the bucket, and snapshots a volume's backup folder and its moments folder, tagged with the moment and the volume; the termination message carries the moment and the bytes sent. The maintenance Job runs kopia maintenance run --full, and with a Compliance lock first turns on lock extension. Keys come from Secrets, never in the script or its arguments (part 3 replaced the backup key's environment variable with the Key Protect unwrap). A Compliance keep time shorter than the maintenance interval plus 24 hours is refused. Tested against a Kopia repository in a folder; the MinIO test runs only when MINIO_ENDPOINT is set. Spec: docs/specs/2026-10-21-backup-cos-export.md.
  • A snapshot pool can have more than one share (issue #71). A new volume is backed up to the ready share that has room and holds the fewest volumes; its backups stay on that share for good, and a restore reads from it (shareID in the volume's status; an entry made before this change belongs to the first share). A policy makes one replication policy for each source pool and share. The 85% limit works for each share: only the copies to a full share stop, and new volumes avoid it. A new volume that no share can take waits and says so. The metric vpc_file_pool_backup_snapshot_pool_used_percent has a new label share. kubectl backup delete reads the share from the status; for a deleted policy, --share names it when the pool has more than one.
  • Backups stop when the snapshot pool is more than 85% full (issue #69). A small Job on the snapshot share reads its usage (df) about every 10 minutes. Above 85%, the BackupPolicy goes to Error with the usage in status.message, and its owned ReplicationPolicy objects get the paused annotation (as suspend does). Backups are never deleted to make room, and resume when usage falls to 85% or less. New metric vpc_file_pool_backup_snapshot_pool_used_percent; alert rules in MONITORING.md.
  • kubectl backup delete --policy P --pvc NS/NAME [--yes] removes the backup folder and the earlier moments of one volume from the snapshot pool, with a Job on the pool's share. It shows the paths and the size and asks for a typed confirmation first; --yes is required in a shell that is not interactive. It refuses while the policy still backs up the volume or a restore of it runs. The controller never runs it. A deleted policy needs --pool and --volume (issue #70).
  • Instant VM disk snapshots (Experimental). Where the KubeVirt Sidecar feature gate is on, a snapshot of a VM disk is a new overlay file, as in VMware: nothing is copied, and the snapshot is ready in seconds whatever the disk size. It is taken inside CreateSnapshot, so an OpenShift VM snapshot gives every disk of a VM at the moment OpenShift froze the guest; before, each disk was copied later, one after another (issue #14). Deleting a snapshot merges its file while the VM runs. Restoring is one sparse qemu-img convert. A mutating webhook gives a VM with snapshots the driver's hook when it starts; frozen files are read-only, so a VM that starts without the hook fails safe. New: Helm vmSnapshots.method and vmSnapshots.launcherImage, flags --vm-snapshot-method and --virt-launcher-image, SubVolume status.diskChain and status.chainOperation, Snapshot status.chainFile, status.mergeChild and status.methodReason, and the kubectl pool-snapshots flatten plugin (make build-pool-snapshots). Design and lab results: VM-INSTANT-SNAPSHOTS.md.
  • Release test stage 18 (backup to a snapshot pool): runs test/e2e/test-backup.sh and checks each outcome it logs. Not run on a cluster yet. remote.sh now also builds kubectl-backup and ships all of test/e2e (stage 6 needs test-vm-snapshot.sh there).

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Group snapshots are no longer shown as a working feature (#100). Nothing acts on a VolumeGroupSnapshot and the hooks never ran, so the docs now say "not active" and the console no longer has the Group Snapshots tab or its pages. The code and the record type stay.
  • Docs no longer say the VPC API has no share snapshot operation. It has one. The driver does not use it, because a share holds many volumes (#101).
  • The console dashboard no longer shows "NaN ms" and a red "High" when there were no allocations. No data now shows "-" with no label (#113).
  • Console plugin libraries updated: advisories down from over 60 to 14. The 14 left are build tools or have no fix; each is listed with its reason in osv-scanner.toml and expires on 2026-12-31. Go libraries mongo-driver and x/crypto updated too. New CI job "Dependency scan" fails on any other known advisory (#90).
  • kubectl backup and kubectl failover now use the KUBECONFIG variable when --kubeconfig is not given, as kubectl does. Before, they read only ~/.kube/config.
  • A backup policy with a longer name could not copy plain volumes. The name of the replication policy a backup policy makes (backup-<policy>-<pool>-<hash>) is a label value on the temporary volume of a copy, and it went over 63 characters for a policy and pool name of about 25 characters each. The copy failed on every cycle with "must be no more than 63 characters", and the VM disks, which use another path, still worked. The name is now cut to fit; names that already fit stay as they were. Found by release stage 18 on the lab.
  • A VM disk made by a CDI clone (for example a VM from the OpenShift console catalog) is now seen as the VM's disk. CDI provisions the clone through a temporary claim and then binds the volume to the VM's claim; the SubVolume kept the temporary claim. The driver then did not find the running VM, so a snapshot of a running VM's disk was a plain file copy, not an instant or QEMU snapshot. A new controller sets the SubVolume's claim to the claim its volume is bound to, also for volumes that exist already.
  • A slow snapshot, snapshot delete or restore no longer makes every other volume's create and delete wait. Each of these calls now locks only the volume it changes; the driver-wide lock is held just for the share's space bookkeeping. Two changes to the same disk still never run at once (issue #99).
  • Deleting a pool no longer deletes the data of its snapshots. The pool waits while snapshots exist (DeletionBlocked reason SnapshotsExist), and a drained share counts its snapshots too (new status.drainStatus[].remainingSnapshots). A snapshot whose pool an older driver already deleted can now be deleted; before, its delete was stuck for ever (issue #96).
  • A snapshot's space charge on its share now survives the pool's regular recount; before, the next reconcile dropped it, and the later delete then counted the share too low. A snapshot no longer counts as a PVC, and a share that has no room for a snapshot refuses it with ResourceExhausted instead of being over-committed (issue #97).
  • A restore into a volume smaller than the snapshot is refused (OutOfRange) instead of making a volume the data does not fit in (issue #98).
  • Replication finds a VM disk whose top file is not disk.img.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• VMs now come from the standard OpenShift Virtualization catalog. Pick a catalog image and choose the pool's StorageClass for the boot disk. CDI copies the image onto the pool. The controller keeps the memory limit of CDI's copy pods at least 8Gi, through HyperConverged spec.resourceRequirements.storageWorkloads. CDI's default of 600 MB is too small for copies onto NFS: the pod is killed. Measured on rovslab on 20 October 2026: a 25 GB copy with a 2Gi limit was killed 6 times and never finished. With 8Gi it finished in 134 s and the checksum matched. A RHEL 9 catalog VM on a pool had its guest agent after 103 s.
  • Golden images are hidden from the console pool form. The pool form no longer offers them, and the "VM storage" preset no longer turns them on. The code is kept for possible later use, and spec.goldenImages still works if a pool sets it in YAML. The standard catalog is the recommended way.
  • The release test makes its VMs from the standard catalog (stage 08), copies 25 GB from Ceph with CDI and checks the checksum, and checks CDI's copy pod limit in stage 01.
  • Release test stage 16 restores a snapshot to a new claim in a real browser (issue #45, part 2). A second console runs with a write token that works in the test namespace only; the read-only token for the first browser run is unchanged. The stage then reads the new claim from a pod and checks the files against the data at snapshot time.
  • CDI clones onto a pool are made by the driver. The pool's CDI StorageProfile now sets cloneStrategy: csi-clone instead of copy. CDI's host-assisted copy pods (memory limit 600 MB) were killed for lack of memory when they wrote onto NFS: 3 of 3 copies on rovslab, onto a pool and onto IBM VPC File alike. Copying a catalog image from other storage, such as Ceph, onto a pool still uses those pods. They now have a higher memory limit (see below).
  • Golden images are imported by CDI. The syncer now makes a CDI DataVolume golden-<image> in each target namespace, on the pool's StorageClass, with the DataImportCron's registry URL as source (pullMethod: node). For ImageStream-based crons (RHEL), it uses the external address the ImageStream imports from. A golden image is ready when the DataVolume phase is Succeeded. On rovslab, CentOS Stream 9 imported in about 40 s and RHEL 9 in about 2.5 min, and VMs booted from both. Catalog entries (DataSources) are now named <image>-<namespace>-nfs-pool, one per golden claim. Two pools must not send golden images to the same namespace.
  • Shares use security group access mode. IBM has deprecated VPC access mode (End of Support 6 May 2027), and the VPC API now refuses new VPC-mode mount targets with HTTP 501, so the driver could not create usable storage on a new cluster. Each share now gets one mount target with a virtual network interface in the worker subnet of the pool's zone, protected by the cluster security group kube-<cluster ID>.
  • The controller reads every subnet in vpc_subnet_ids (and --subnet-id accepts a comma-separated list) and picks the one in each pool's zone. It used to take the first subnet, whatever its zone.
  • A pool is Ready only when at least one share is stable and has a mount target address. Otherwise it is Degraded, and the SharesReady condition (reason NoMountTarget) names the shares. Pools do not add shares while a share is still being created or has no mount target.
  • accessorZones[].subnetID is now optional and not used: one mount target in the home zone serves every zone.
  • metrics.serviceMonitor.enabled is now true by default. The chart creates the ServiceMonitor only when the cluster has the Prometheus Operator API, so installs on other clusters still work.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Console: VM copy settings on the replication policy. The create form has the VM copy speed limit (MB/s per disk, default 20, 0 for unlimited) and the restore point keep time (hours, default 24). The details page shows both, with the defaults named. Part of #46 (item 2).
  • Snapshots of the disks of a running VM show one moment (#14). The driver now copies all the pool disks of a VM with QEMU at one moment when the first disk's snapshot starts, and the snapshots KubeVirt asks for the other disks join that copy (same status.copyMoment and status.copyID). Before, each disk was copied on its own turn: in a lab test on 21 October 2026 the two disks of a VM were copied 80 s apart, and 725 of 1,154 logged files were missing on the second disk after a restore. A snapshot of one disk of a multi-disk VM now also copies the other disks to temporary files, which are deleted after 10 minutes if no snapshot claims them. New status fields copyID, vmCopySet and vmCopy.leader. New e2e test test/e2e/test-vm-snapshot-2disk.sh and a check in release stage 06.
  • Backup to a snapshot pool (step 8 of the VM-safe replication plan). New resources BackupPolicy and BackupRestore. A BackupPolicy selects PVCs by label (a VM is backed up with all its disks) and keeps one owned ReplicationPolicy for each source pool, aimed at a pool that holds only backups. VM disks are backed up at one moment, change-only, with restore points for keepFor (default 7 days); other volumes keep each sync as a folder of hard links (new ReplicationPolicy field momentKeepHours). kubectl backup list and kubectl backup restore (new plugin, make build-backup) show the moments and restore any of them to a new PVC, also after the source volume is gone. A new PVC is held back from pods until its copy ends (label storage.ibmcloud.io/restore-pending, checked by the node plugin). New driver mode restore-vm-disk, new metrics vpc_file_pool_backup_volumes, vpc_file_pool_backup_stalest_age_seconds and vpc_file_pool_backup_oldest_age_seconds, a webhook for each new resource, and RBAC to read VirtualMachines. Not yet: more than one share in the snapshot pool (#71), a stop at 85% full (#69), a command to remove backups (#70), export to COS. While a snapshot copies a VM, replication of that VM waits.
  • Snapshots of running VM disks are made with a QEMU copy. If a running VM uses the claim, CreateSnapshot no longer copies the file while the VM writes to it. The controller freezes the guest, has QEMU copy the disk at one moment, and a Job writes a raw disk.img into the snapshot folder. status.consistency says FileSystemConsistent or CrashConsistent, and status.copyMoment names the moment. A migration cancels the copy; it is tried again up to 3 times. New VolumeSnapshotClass parameter vmCopySpeedLimitMBps (default 20). A snapshot covers one disk. While a snapshot copies a VM, replication of that VM waits, and the other way round (vmcopy.CheckIdle, vmcopy.ErrBusy). New e2e test test/e2e/test-vm-snapshot.sh.
  • Running VM replication tested across two clusters, with Windows. test/e2e/test-vm-replication.sh takes DR_KUBECONFIG (destination pool, receiver behind a Route, far-site disks and copy VMs on the second cluster) and GUEST=windows (Windows Server 2022 from an existing Windows disk, checked through the guest agent). Lab result, 21 October 2026: both guest types copy at one moment (FileSystemConsistent), boot at the destination, and every logged file matches its checksum, at the latest moment and after a rewind.
  • Console: delete the receiver setup's Secrets with a policy (#67). The delete dialog of a ReplicationPolicy has an extra box, off by default, to also delete <policy>-receiver-token and <policy>-receiver-ca in kube-system when the console made them and no other policy uses them. A Secret without the console's label is left alone. If the policy is deleted but a Secret cannot be, the dialog says so before it closes.
  • Console: receiver setup with a connection check (#46, item 4). In Driver-to-Driver mode the replication form makes the token and CA Secrets (<policy>-receiver-token, <policy>-receiver-ca) from what you paste, or uses existing ones, and a "Check connection" button runs a one-shot Job in kube-system (--mode=check-receiver) that tests the address, the certificate and the token. Create stays off until it passes. The check Job is built by the same code in Go and TypeScript, tied together by a golden file (pkg/replication/testdata/check-job.golden.json).
  • Receiver check (driver side of the console's receiver setup, #46 item 4). The receiver has a new read-only call, GET /api/v1/auth-check: it needs the bearer token and returns 200 when the token is accepted and the receiver's storage is reachable. A new driver mode, --mode=check-receiver, uses it: it tests the address, the certificate and the token in that order, prints one result line (ok, cannot connect, certificate not trusted, token refused, receiver storage not reachable, or receiver has no auth-check call; update it), writes it to the termination log, and exits 1 on a failure. The console form comes next.
  • Console: panels for the group snapshot and CDI metrics. A collapsed "Group Snapshot and CDI Activity" section on the Monitoring tab charts the group snapshot inconsistency window (P95), the average members per group snapshot, and the times the controller raised CDI's copy limit (a raise after start-up means something reset it). Part of #46 (item 8).
  • Console: migrate volumes into a pool. A "Migrate volumes into a pool" page, linked from the Pools tab. It lists the claims of another storage class, turns Migrate off for a claim a pod uses or a move that does not fit the pool, asks for confirmation, and makes the same new claim (<name>-pooled) and pod as kubectl migrate execute. It shows the copy and never deletes the old claim. A golden file (pkg/migrate/testdata/migration-objects.golden.json) ties the Go and TypeScript builders together. Part of #46 (item 6).
  • Console: clone a volume to a new PVC. A "Clone to new PVC" action on the SubVolume details page and in the list row menu. It makes a claim whose data source is the volume's claim, warns when a VM uses the claim, and shows the copy until the claim is Bound. It shares its form and progress banner with the snapshot restore. Part of #46 (item 7).
  • Console: restore a snapshot to a new PVC. A "Restore to new PVC" action on the snapshot details page and in the list row menu. It makes a claim from the snapshot's VolumeSnapshot, warns when a VM uses the source claim, and shows the copy until the claim is Bound. The console finds the VolumeSnapshot from the VolumeSnapshotContent's snapshotHandle (<pool>/<share ID>/<Snapshot name>).
  • Failover picks one moment for all disks of a running VM. kubectl failover plan and execute choose the newest moment all of a VM's disks can show, roll back a copy that stopped half way, and rewind a disk that is ahead into a new folder. New flags --rewind-to TIME (an earlier restore point), --list-moments and --force. The receiver keeps a lease file while it applies a copy, and failover waits for it.
  • Console: drain a share, and return it to service. The pool page's share table has a "Drain" button on each share, and "Return to service" for a share on the drain list. A confirm dialog says what happens first: new volumes stop going to the share, existing volumes stay until their PVCs are deleted, and no data moves. The return dialog warns that a share you plan to delete must stay on the list until it is gone. Part of #46 (item 5).
  • A pool whose share size and IOPS do not fit IBM's rules is refused at once. The FileSharePool admission check (also for each tier) now checks IOPS against IBM's table for the share size, and says which range is allowed. Before, IBM refused it later with shares_profile_capacity_iops_invalid, as a slow background error. An empty iops is still allowed.
  • Console: replication status for running VMs. The replication policy page now shows, for each volume, the moment the last copy shows, whether it is file-system or crash consistent (with the reason), the restore points and the oldest one, whether the next copy holds changes only or is full, and the phase of a copy in progress. A message that only says a volume is waiting ("skipped: in use by running VM", "copy waits", "copy lost") shows as a warning, not an error. Part of #46.
  • Receiver mode copies running VMs too. A send-vm-disk Job sends the QEMU copy to the receiver, which applies it at the destination with the same undo files and restore points as direct NFS mode, so each changed block crosses the network once. After a VM move or restart, only the blocks that differ from the destination disk are sent. New driver mode send-vm-disk and flags --vm-group and --copy-id. New receiver calls under /api/v1/vmcopy/.
  • Running VM copies send only changed blocks, and the destination keeps restore points. After the first copy, QEMU's change list limits each copy to the blocks changed since the last good copy; after a VM restart or move the next copy is full. The destination saves the old contents of every block before it changes it, so a copy that stops half way is rolled back and never leaves a mixed disk, and keeps those undo files as restore points for restorePointKeepHours (default 24). Only blocks whose contents differ are written. The status shows restorePoints and oldestRestorePoint for each VM disk. The apply Job's driver mode gains --from, --to, --full and --keep.
  • Helm value cdi.copyPodMemoryLimit (default 8Gi; empty turns the check off) and controller flag --cdi-copy-pod-memory-limit. The controller checks at start-up and every 5 minutes (leader only), and only raises the limit. The controller ClusterRole gets get, list and patch on hco.kubevirt.io hyperconvergeds.
