  2. InProgress: Member snapshots are being created sequentially in copyOrder.
  3. Complete: All member snapshots are Ready.
  4. PartialFailure: Some members succeeded and some failed (only with failurePolicy: Continue).
  5. Failed: The operation failed and was rolled back (with failurePolicy: Abort), or all members failed.

docs.title: BackupPolicy
docs.text:
Cluster-scoped. Backs up the PVCs it selects, and the VMs whose disks it selects, into a pool that holds only backups. The controller labels the SubVolumes it selects (storage.ibmcloud.io/backup-policy) and makes one ReplicationPolicy for each source pool (backup-<policy>-<pool>, owned by the BackupPolicy), aimed at the snapshot pool's share. Replication does the copying: QEMU for running VM disks at one moment for all disks of a VM, changed blocks only, with restore points for the keep time; other volumes are synced with rsync and each sync is kept as a folder of hard links. Do not edit the owned policies: the controller sets them back.

type BackupPolicySpec struct {
    // SnapshotPool holds the backups. It must hold no workload claims and have at least one ready share.
    SnapshotPool string `json:"snapshotPool"`
    // Schedule is a Go duration of at least 1 minute, such as "6h".
    Schedule string `json:"schedule"`
    // Selector selects PVCs by label. A VM is selected through its disks: if any disk matches,
    // all disks of the VM are backed up. An empty selector is refused.
    Selector *metav1.LabelSelector `json:"selector"`
    // Namespaces limits the PVCs to these namespaces. Empty means all.
    Namespaces []string `json:"namespaces,omitempty"`
    // KeepFor is a Go duration or a number of days ("30d"), at least one hour. Default "7d".
    KeepFor string `json:"keepFor,omitempty"`
    // VMCopySpeedLimitMBps is the highest speed of the QEMU copy of each VM disk, in MB/s.
    // 0 or unset means there is no highest speed. With VMCopyAdaptive false it is the fixed
    // speed: 0 means no limit and unset means 20.
    VMCopySpeedLimitMBps *int32 `json:"vmCopySpeedLimitMBps,omitempty"`
    // VMCopyAdaptive starts the copy slow, speeds it up while the source share is quiet and slows
    // it down when the share's latency passes VMCopyMaxLatencyMs. Default true.
    VMCopyAdaptive *bool `json:"vmCopyAdaptive,omitempty"`
    // VMCopyMaxLatencyMs is the share latency in ms above which the copy slows down. Default 15; 1 to 20.
    VMCopyMaxLatencyMs *int32 `json:"vmCopyMaxLatencyMs,omitempty"`
    // Suspend stops new backups. Existing backups stay.
    Suspend bool `json:"suspend,omitempty"`
    // Export also sends the backups to an IBM Cloud Object Storage bucket (see below). Optional.
    Export *BackupExport `json:"export,omitempty"`
}

type BackupExport struct {
    Bucket   string `json:"bucket"`             // the COS bucket
    Endpoint string `json:"endpoint"`           // S3 host, e.g. s3.eu-de.cloud-object-storage.appdomain.cloud
    Prefix   string `json:"prefix,omitempty"`   // folder in the bucket; the policy's own area is <prefix>/<policy>/
    // CredentialsSecret names a Secret in the driver namespace with the driver's COS HMAC key:
    // access_key_id and secret_access_key.
    CredentialsSecret string `json:"credentialsSecret"`
    // BackupKeySecret names a Secret in the driver namespace with the backup key, wrapped
    // by Key Protect (key "wrappedKey"). The readable key is never stored. Only the Jobs read
    // the Secret, never the controller; a Job asks Key Protect to unwrap the key and keeps it
    // in memory.
    BackupKeySecret string `json:"backupKeySecret"`
    // KeyProtect says which root key unwraps the backup key. All four fields are required.
    KeyProtect KeyProtectRef `json:"keyProtect"`
    // EmergencyKeySecret is optional: a Secret (key "backupKey") with the readable backup key,
    // used only when Key Protect cannot be reached.
    EmergencyKeySecret string `json:"emergencyKeySecret,omitempty"`
    // KeepFor is a Go duration or a number of days. Default "30d". At least one hour; with a
    // Compliance lock, at least 25 hours.
    KeepFor string `json:"keepFor,omitempty"`
    // Lock is "Compliance" (default: nobody can delete or shorten the keep time) or "None".
    Lock string `json:"lock,omitempty"`
    // Schedule is a Go duration of at least 1 minute: the most often a volume is sent.
    // Empty: after each local backup.
    Schedule string `json:"schedule,omitempty"`
}

type KeyProtectRef struct {
    InstanceID   string `json:"instanceID"`   // GUID of the Key Protect instance
    Region       string `json:"region"`       // e.g. eu-de
    RootKeyID    string `json:"rootKeyID"`    // the root key that wrapped the backup key
    // APIKeySecret names a Secret (key "apikey") with an IBM Cloud API key that has the Reader
    // role on the root key.
    APIKeySecret string `json:"apiKeySecret"`
}

Status: phase (Active, Suspended, Error; Error is also set, with the usage in message, while the snapshot pool's share is more than 85% full and new backups are stopped), message, volumeCount, replicationPolicies, and volumes. Each volume has the claim, the VM, lastBackupTime, oldestBackupTime, restorePoints (moments before the newest that can be restored), bytesWritten, consistency (FileSystemConsistent or CrashConsistent for a VM disk, FileCopy for any other volume) and lastError. It also keeps what a restore needs (subPath, requestedGB, storageClassName). A volume that was deleted, or no longer matches the selector, stays in the list with retained: true until the keep time has passed since its last backup.

Export to COS. With spec.export, when the local backup of a volume has a moment newer than the last one exported, the controller starts an export Job for the volume (one at a time for each policy). The Job mounts the snapshot pool's share read-only and sends the backup folder and the moments folder to a Kopia repository in the bucket, in the area <prefix>/<policy>/. Each volume's status then has exportedTime (the moment of the newest copy in COS), exportedBytes (what the last export sent) and exportError (the last error; the export is tried again after 5 minutes). Once a volume is exported, a maintenance Job runs once every maintenance interval (a day, or less for a short keep time; one hour at the least): it extends the locks of chunks still in use and deletes the Kopia snapshots older than keepFor. The rule for the shortest Compliance lock is in one helper (v1alpha1.MinComplianceKeepFor): the keep time must be at least the maintenance interval plus 24 hours, so 25 hours at the least; the webhook and the controller both use it. An export problem never changes phase and never stops the backups to the snapshot pool. Removing spec.export clears the three export fields; backups already in COS stay until their lock ends. Key handling. The backup key is stored only as a Key Protect-wrapped copy (in backupKeySecret, and next to the backups in the bucket). Each export and maintenance Job mounts the wrapped key, the API key and the optional emergency key as read-only Secret files, runs the driver in mode unwrap-backup-key (which asks Key Protect to unwrap the key and writes it, mode 0400, to a memory-backed folder), lets Kopia read it, and removes the file. The controller never reads these Secrets and never calls Key Protect. If Key Protect is unreachable and emergencyKeySecret is set, the Job uses that key and logs that it did; a refusal from Key Protect (a wrong root key, a bad API key) is an error and never falls back. kubectl backup cos-setup makes the wrapped key; see'; see docs/specs/2026-10-21-backup-cos-export.md.

A volume belongs to one policy. A second policy that selects it skips it and says so in its message. The policy name goes into a label value, so it has at most 63 characters.

Each entry of status.volumes[] names the claim (pvcNamespace, pvcName), its SubVolume (subVolumeName) and, for a VM disk, the VM (vmName).

A snapshot pool may have several shares. A volume gets a share when it is first backed up (the one with room that holds the fewest volumes) and keeps it; status.volumes[].shareID names it, and a restore reads from it. An entry with no shareID was made when the pool had one share and belongs to the first share. A policy makes one ReplicationPolicy for each source pool and share (the SubVolumes carry storage.ibmcloud.io/backup-share). A new volume that no ready share below 85% can take waits, with its lastError saying so.

docs.title: BackupRestore
docs.text:
Cluster-scoped. A request to make a new PVC from a backup. kubectl backup restore makes one.

type BackupRestoreSpec struct {
    Policy          string        `json:"policy"`
    SourceNamespace string        `json:"sourceNamespace,omitempty"` // the claim that was backed up; it may be gone. Required unless fromCOS is set
    SourceName      string        `json:"sourceName,omitempty"`
    Moment          *metav1.Time  `json:"moment,omitempty"` // the newest backup at or before it; unset: the latest
    TargetNamespace string        `json:"targetNamespace"`  // the new PVC; it must not exist
    TargetName      string        `json:"targetName"`
    StorageClassName string       `json:"storageClassName,omitempty"` // default: the class of the backed-up claim; required with fromCOS
    FromCOS         *RestoreFromCOS `json:"fromCOS,omitempty"` // read the backup from a COS bucket, not from a snapshot pool
}

// RestoreFromCOS needs no BackupPolicy and no snapshot pool in this cluster.
type RestoreFromCOS struct {
    Bucket             string          `json:"bucket"`
    Endpoint           string          `json:"endpoint"`
    Prefix             string          `json:"prefix,omitempty"`             // the prefix set in the policy's spec.export; spec.policy names the policy's area below it
    CredentialsSecret  string          `json:"credentialsSecret"`            // access_key_id, secret_access_key
    Volume             string          `json:"volume"`                       // pvc-<uuid>, as `kubectl backup cos-list` shows it
    SizeGB             int32           `json:"sizeGB"`                       // size of the new PVC; COS does not keep it
    BackupKeySecret    string          `json:"backupKeySecret,omitempty"`    // key wrappedKey; not used with emergencyKeyOnly
    KeyProtect         *KeyProtectRef  `json:"keyProtect,omitempty"`         // not used with emergencyKeyOnly
    EmergencyKeySecret string          `json:"emergencyKeySecret,omitempty"` // key backupKey: the readable backup key
    EmergencyKeyOnly   bool            `json:"emergencyKeyOnly,omitempty"`   // never call Key Protect
}

The controller makes the PVC (like the backed-up claim: same size, ReadWriteMany, Filesystem), waits for the driver to bind it, and runs a Job that copies the backup into it. Until the copy ends, the SubVolume carries the label storage.ibmcloud.io/restore-pending and the node plugin refuses to mount the volume, so no pod or VM sees a half-written disk. A VM disk is written by the driver's restore-vm-disk mode, which rewinds it to the moment; the Job never rolls back a copy that is being written (the restore waits and says so). Status: phase (Pending, Provisioning, Restoring, Done, Failed), message, restoredMoment and latest. A restore never writes over a volume that exists; a failed copy leaves the new PVC held back, and you delete it and ask again.

With spec.fromCOS the backup comes from the Kopia repository in a COS bucket (kubectl backup restore --from-cos). spec.policy names the policy's area in the bucket (below fromCOS.prefix); the policy need not exist in the cluster. The new PVC gets spec.storageClassName and fromCOS.sizeGB, because COS keeps neither. Three Jobs run on the share of the new volume: one opens the repository read-only and restores the export for the moment into a scratch folder (/backup/cosrestore-<name> on that share), the restore Job of a local restore copies the scratch folder into the volume, and a third removes the scratch folder. spec.moment picks the oldest export made at or after it (it holds the earlier moments as undo files), or the newest export if there is none; the existing restore Job then picks the moment inside it. Status adds fetched and copied, which record the finished steps because a finished Job is removed. The scratch folder needs room for one full copy of the volume on the share. The webhook requires storageClassName, a pvc-<uuid> volume, a sizeGB, and either backupKeySecret with keyProtect or emergencyKeyOnly with emergencyKeySecret. A scratch folder that cannot be removed is logged and left; the restore is still Done.

docs.title: BackupBrowse
docs.text:
Cluster-scoped. One open session on one backup of one volume, for browsing files (issue #92). Users never make or see it: the backup gateway makes it after it checks the user's rights, and the backup controller runs it. Short name bb.

type BackupBrowseSpec struct {
    Policy       string       `json:"policy"`
    PVCNamespace string       `json:"pvcNamespace"`           // the claim that was backed up; it may be gone
    PVCName      string       `json:"pvcName"`
    Moment       *metav1.Time `json:"moment,omitempty"`       // the newest backup at or before it; unset: the latest copy
    RequestedBy  string       `json:"requestedBy,omitempty"`  // the user, for the audit trail; decides nothing
    Source       string       `json:"source,omitempty"`       // local (the snapshot pool, the default) or cos (the policy's export bucket)
    FromCOS      *BrowseFromCOS `json:"fromCOS,omitempty"`    // a bucket named directly (a cluster administrator); source must be cos
    Guest        bool         `json:"guest,omitempty"`        // read the file systems inside a VM disk (the volume must be a VM disk); holds the disk's next backup copy
    Close        bool         `json:"close,omitempty"`        // end the session
}

type BackupBrowseStatus struct {
    Phase      string       `json:"phase,omitempty"`      // Pending, Starting, Ready, Closed, Failed
    Message    string       `json:"message,omitempty"`
    PodIP      string       `json:"podIP,omitempty"`      // where the helper answers, over TLS
    Port       int32        `json:"port,omitempty"`
    SecretName string       `json:"secretName,omitempty"` // token, tls.crt, tls.key; owned by this resource
    StartedTime *metav1.Time `json:"startedTime,omitempty"` // when the helper was started; a COS session fails if it is not ready 5 minutes later
    EndReason  string       `json:"endReason,omitempty"`  // idle, max-life, closed, stopped
    EndedTime  *metav1.Time `json:"endedTime,omitempty"`
}

For each session the controller makes a Secret with a random token and a new self-signed TLS certificate and key, and a Job whose one pod (the browse image) mounts only this volume's backup folder, and its moments folder if it has earlier moments, read-only down to the NFS export. The pod has no service account token, runs as root with every capability dropped on a read-only root file system, and serves its API over TLS. The gateway trusts exactly that certificate. Every object of a session (Job, share volume and claim, Secret) is named and labelled with the UID of the BackupBrowse, never its name, and owned by it, so a session deleted and made again with the same name cannot get the old session's Secret or pod, which still mounts the old volume.

With spec.source: cos the session reads the Kopia repository in the COS bucket that the policy's spec.export names (the volume is the one the policy keeps for the claim), or, with spec.fromCOS, the bucket the block names (bucket, endpoint, prefix, credentialsSecret, volume, backupKeySecret, keyProtect, emergencyKeySecret, emergencyKeyOnly; the same checks as BackupRestore.spec.fromCOS, and the endpoint must be a COS S3 host). For fromCOS, spec.policy is the policy's area in the bucket and pvcNamespace and pvcName hold - and the volume. The helper pod runs in the driver namespace, next to the COS and Key Protect Secrets, which the controller never reads (it checks from their metadata that they exist, and fails the session in words if one does not). It mounts no share, has no service account token and runs as an ordinary user. The controller keeps a copy of the session Secret in the driver namespace for it to mount; the gateway reads only the one in the browse namespace. A helper that stops with an error puts its reason in the termination log, and the status message shows it. A COS session whose helper is not ready after five minutes ends as Failed with a message that names the Secrets to check.

With spec.guest the session reads the file systems inside a VM disk (issue #92, phase 5). The volume must be a VM disk (the policy status names its VM) and the backup must be in the snapshot pool; the guest helper image must be set, or the session fails in words. The disk's backup folder holds disk.img and the undo files of its earlier moments, so there is no moments folder: the helper rebuilds the view at spec.moment from them, read-only. While the session is Pending, Starting or Ready it holds the disk: the controller adds the session's UID to the annotation storage.ibmcloud.io/browse-hold on the volume's SubVolume before it starts the helper, waits while a backup copy of the disk is running, and removes the entry when the helper is gone or the session no longer exists. The replication controller starts no new copy of a held volume (held: waiting for a browse session).

A session ends when the helper stops by itself (idle, default 15 minutes), when it is 2 hours old (the hard limit, counted from creation, so a controller restart does not extend it), when spec.close is set, or when the helper fails. The controller stops the Job, removes the Secret, and removes the record 10 minutes later. Pending means the session waits for a free slot (5 in the cluster and 2 for the claims of one namespace by default) or for a ready share in the snapshot pool. A request for a policy or a claim that has no backup fails at once. A moment before the first earlier moment, or any moment of a volume with no earlier moments yet, reads the latest copy, as a restore does. Helper Jobs and Secrets whose session is gone are removed on the next pass, also after a restart. See docs/specs/2026-10-22-backup-file-restore.md.

docs.title: BackupFileRestore
docs.text:
Cluster-scoped. Copies chosen files and folders out of one backup into a claim: a new claim, or a new folder in an existing claim (issue #92). The backup gateway makes it for a user after it checks the user's rights (kubectl backup restore-files); a cluster administrator may make one by hand. Short name bfr. The webhook refuses a change to the spec.

type BackupFileRestoreSpec struct {
    Policy           string       `json:"policy"`
    SourceNamespace  string       `json:"sourceNamespace"`           // the claim that was backed up; it may be gone
    SourceName       string       `json:"sourceName"`
    Moment           *metav1.Time `json:"moment,omitempty"`          // the newest backup at or before it; unset: the latest copy
    Source           string       `json:"source,omitempty"`          // local (the default) or cos
    FromCOS          *BrowseFromCOS `json:"fromCOS,omitempty"`       // a bucket named directly (a cluster administrator); sourceNamespace holds "-", sourceName the volume, storageClassName is required for a new claim
    Guest            bool         `json:"guest,omitempty"`           // restore files from inside a VM disk; the first name of each path is a file system of the guest
    Paths            []string     `json:"paths"`                     // 1 to 1000, escaped form ("\\" and "\xNN"); "/" is the whole volume
    TargetNamespace  string       `json:"targetNamespace"`
    TargetName       string       `json:"targetName"`
    Existing         bool         `json:"existing,omitempty"`        // false: a new claim; true: a new folder in the claim
    SizeGB           int64        `json:"sizeGB,omitempty"`          // new claim only; unset: the files plus 20%, at least 1
    StorageClassName string       `json:"storageClassName,omitempty"` // new claim only; unset: the class of the backed-up claim
    TargetUID        types.UID    `json:"targetUID,omitempty"`       // existing claim only; the gateway sets it
    RequestedBy      string       `json:"requestedBy,omitempty"`     // the user, for the audit trail; decides nothing
}

type BackupFileRestoreStatus struct {
    Phase          string       `json:"phase,omitempty"`   // Pending, Measuring, Provisioning, Restoring, Done, Failed
    Message        string       `json:"message,omitempty"`
    TargetUID      types.UID    `json:"targetUID,omitempty"` // the claim this restore writes to; another UID is refused
    GuestHoldStarted *metav1.Time `json:"guestHoldStarted,omitempty"` // when a guest restore first held its VM disk; never moved, the restore fails 2h45m after it
    SizeGB         int64        `json:"sizeGB,omitempty"`    // the size chosen for a new claim
    Folder         string       `json:"folder,omitempty"`    // the folder made in an existing claim
    RestoredMoment *metav1.Time `json:"restoredMoment,omitempty"`
    Latest         bool         `json:"latest,omitempty"`
    Files          int          `json:"files,omitempty"`      // what was written
    Dirs           int          `json:"dirs,omitempty"`
    Links          int          `json:"links,omitempty"`
    Skipped        int          `json:"skipped,omitempty"`    // devices, pipes and sockets left out
    Unreadable     int          `json:"unreadable,omitempty"` // entries the reader could not read
    Bytes          int64        `json:"bytes,omitempty"`
    EndedTime      *metav1.Time `json:"endedTime,omitempty"`
}

With spec.guest the volume must be a VM disk in the snapshot pool (not COS; the webhook and the controller refuse it). The Job runs in the guest image with the program browse --mode=restore-files, which has the same restore code, and reads the file systems inside disk.img through the read-only appliance, as a guest browse session does. The first name of each path is the file system (/sda1/etc/hosts) and it is kept in the restored tree (sda1/etc/hosts in the new claim). The pod has two containers, because the reader parses a disk that someone else controlled. The reader is like the guest helper (two size-limited scratch folders, 1 CPU and 1 GiB, the KVM device if configured): it mounts the backup read-only, has no capability and cannot write the target. The writer (browse --mode=restore-writer, same image) mounts only the target and holds only CHOWN and FOWNER; it never sees the disk. They talk over a private socket in a shared small folder. The writer takes the target, the owner and the limits from its own command line, checks every path again, counts the bytes itself, always sets the owner of its own spec (the claim's UID and GID; if the SubVolume has none, a new claim gets the pool's defaults and an existing claim gets the owner its folder has when the writer starts, read before any data is accepted; with none of these the restore fails with "the owner of the target claim is not known") and never the reader's, keeps only the permission bits 0777 (no setuid, setgid or sticky bit), sets the mode of the root folder itself, limits the content to the smaller of the restore limit and the free space of the target, makes the name of the final folder itself, and removes what it wrote if the reader ends without committing. For a new folder in an existing claim the writer mounts the claim's folder only; for a new claim it mounts the share, because the claim's folder does not exist yet, and makes that folder itself. Each Job has a deadline of at most 2 hours, and the restore as a whole may hold the disk for 2 hours 45 minutes at most, counted from status.guestHoldStarted (kept, never moved): each Job may run only for what is left of that time, and the restore fails in words when it is used up, so the hold can never be taken again after the sweep let it go. The controller adds the restore's UID to the annotation storage.ibmcloud.io/browse-hold on the volume's SubVolume before the first Job, waits while a backup copy of the disk is running (only before the Job starts), and removes the entry when the restore has ended. The restore fails in words if the volume is not a VM disk, or the guest image is not set.

With spec.source: cos (or spec.fromCOS) the Job reads the backup from COS, as a browse session does, and runs in the driver namespace with the COS and Key Protect Secrets mounted as files, no service account token and a read-only root file system. Everything else is the same: the targets, the checks, the owner, the space limit. A new claim takes its class from the policy's record of the volume, or from spec.storageClassName when the bucket is named directly (COS does not keep the class). Each file is one run of the Kopia program (about 0.2 seconds on a local repository; not yet measured against a real bucket), so a restore of many thousands of small files is slow; the Job gets 4 hours.

A path is a list of names below the root of the backed-up volume, written as text: / separates names, a backslash is \\, and a byte that is not text is \xNN (so a name with a newline is \x0a). .., an empty name and a NUL byte are refused. The list is at most 1000 paths, 4096 bytes each, 256 KiB together; the controller keeps it in a ConfigMap that the restore owns and mounts it into the Job as a file.

Into a new claim the controller works in this order: it runs a read-only Job that adds up the size of the chosen files (Measuring, skipped when sizeGB is set; more than the limit, 200 GiB by default, fails the restore), makes the claim with the annotations storage.ibmcloud.io/backup-file-restore and .../backup-file-restore-uid (both must match; a claim that exists is never used), waits for the driver to bind it, holds pods back with the label storage.ibmcloud.io/restore-pending, runs the copy Job (Restoring), saves Done, and only then lets pods have the claim. Into an existing claim there is no sizing and no hold-back: the copy Job writes a hidden staging folder in the claim's folder and renames it to restored-<policy>-<moment> (a suffix if the name exists). The restore refuses a claim whose UID is not the one pinned in spec.targetUID (or, if that is unset, the one first seen), a claim that holds disk.img, a claim being restored, and, while another restore into the same claim has not ended, waits. The Job is named by the UID of the restore, never its name, and owned by it, as are its share objects and the ConfigMap of paths. A restore that has ended is removed after 24 hours. See docs/specs/2026-10-22-backup-file-restore.md and BACKUP-RECOVERY.md.

docs.title: PoolBench
docs.text:
Cluster-scoped. One performance test run: a new pool with one share, and test VMs added in steps until users would notice the share is slow. The PoolBench service (off by default) makes and deletes everything the run needs, in the run's own namespace poolbench-<name>. Short name pb. See docs/specs/2026-10-25-poolbench.md.

type PoolBenchSpec struct {
    Zone           string            `json:"zone,omitempty"`           // default: the zone with the most workers
    Profile        string            `json:"profile,omitempty"`        // dp2 only
    ShareSizeGB    int64             `json:"shareSizeGB"`
    IOPS           int64             `json:"iops"`                     // must fit IBM's dp2 table for the size
    StepVMs        int32             `json:"stepVMs,omitempty"`        // default 15
    MaxVMs         int32             `json:"maxVMs,omitempty"`         // default 90; a whole number of steps, at most 500
    WindowsEvery   *int32            `json:"windowsEvery,omitempty"`   // default 3; 0: Linux only
    Linux          PoolBenchVM       `json:"linux,omitempty"`          // cpu, memoryGiB, image, imageNamespace, preference, rootDiskGiB
    Windows        PoolBenchVM       `json:"windows,omitempty"`
    Load           PoolBenchLoad     `json:"load,omitempty"`           // steadyIOPS 30, burstIOPS 300, burstSeconds 45, periodSeconds 600, readPercent 70, blockMix "4k:50 16k:30 64k:20", areaGiB 3
    SettleMinutes  *int32            `json:"settleMinutes,omitempty"`  // default 15
    MeasureMinutes int32             `json:"measureMinutes,omitempty"` // default 45; at least 2 x period - burst seconds
    Knee           PoolBenchKnee     `json:"knee,omitempty"`           // latencyLimitMs 20, slowVMPercent 25, stallSeconds 5, stopAtKnee (default true)
    Events         []PoolBenchEvent  `json:"events,omitempty"`         // type BootStorm, PatchWindow, Migration, Snapshot or Backup; atVMs: a step of the run
    StartAfter     string            `json:"startAfter,omitempty"`     // wait until this other run has ended (a series of tiers)
    KeepAfterEnd   bool              `json:"keepAfterEnd,omitempty"`   // keep the VMs and pool after the end
    Control        PoolBenchControl  `json:"control,omitempty"`        // paused, hold, stop, skipStep, extendStep, extendMinutes
}

type PoolBenchStatus struct {
    Phase          string                 `json:"phase,omitempty"`  // Pending, Checking, Running, Paused, CleaningUp, Complete, Stopped, Failed
    Stage          string                 `json:"stage,omitempty"`  // Preparing, Creating, Settling, Measuring, Event
    Step, TotalSteps                      int32
    VMs, WindowsVMs, ReadyVMs             int32
    Namespace, PoolName                   string
    StartTime, EndTime, StageStarted, StageEnds, PausedAt *metav1.Time
    ShareAtStart, ShareAtEnd *PoolBenchCounters // the share's NFS counters (ops, micros, at) at the start and end of the measuring
    Message        string
    Steps          []PoolBenchStepResult  // one per step: vms, share, guest and IBM IOPS, share latency, p50/p95/p99, throughput, slow %, burst slow %, stalls, at limit, time to ready, pass, cutShort
    KneeVMs        int32                  // the first failed step; 0: no knee
    RecommendedVMs int32                  // 80% of the knee, down to a step; or the largest passed step
    Events         []PoolBenchEventResult // a backup event also has copySpeedAvgMBps and copySpeedMaxMBps (running-VM copies), p95Micros and p95BeforeMicros (the VMs' latency during the event and in the step before)
    Log            []PoolBenchLogEntry    // the newest entries: Info, Warning, Error, Control
    CleanedUp      bool                   // the VMs, pool and namespace are gone and the VPC no longer lists the share
}

The webhook refuses a share size or IOPS outside IBM's dp2 table, a share too small for the disks of the largest step (each VM has its root disk and a load disk one GiB larger than its test area), a load that is not a steady rate and a longer, faster burst, a block mix whose shares do not add up to 100, and an event that is not at a step of the run. The name may be at most 40 characters, so the run's namespace fits a label value. Once the run has started, only spec.control may change, and events may only be added (the console adds one to run an event now).

How a run goes. With spec.startAfter, the run stays Pending until the named run has ended and cleaned up (a run that does not exist holds nothing). Checking: the images must exist and the largest step must fit the workers' free memory with one node down; if not, the run fails and makes nothing. Then the service makes the namespace poolbench-<name> (with the run's token, the Linux cloud-init and the Windows config disk as Secrets) and the pool poolbench-<name> (one share of the size and IOPS under test, never grown). For each step: Creating makes the new VMs and waits, up to 60 minutes, until every VM has sent PERF-READY and every disk copy has ended; Settling waits settleMinutes; Measuring reads the share's counters, waits measureMinutes, reads them again, waits 90 seconds for the last results, and writes the step's row. The knee rule is that of the command-line test: more than slowVMPercent of the VMs slow or with a slow burst, any stall, or the share at 95% of its IOPS limit. At the knee (unless stopAtKnee is false) or after the last step the run cleans up: it deletes the namespace, then the pool, and ends Complete (or Stopped after control.stop). A failed run also cleans up and stays Failed. control.paused stops the clock, and each VM asks the service before each load phase and waits while the run is paused. Deleting a PoolBench cleans up first (finalizer storage.ibmcloud.io/poolbench) and then forgets its results.

docs.title: ReplicationPolicy
docs.text: Cluster-scoped resource. Defines a replication relationship between a source FileSharePool on the local cluster and a destination NFS server for cross-region disaster recovery. In direct NFS mode it uses rsync (incremental) over Transit Gateway or VPN. In receiver mode (destinationEndpoint) it uploads the whole folder as a tar stream each cycle.

docs.title: Go Type Definition
docs.text:
// api/v1alpha1/replicationpolicy_types.go
package v1alpha1

import (
    metav1 "k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1"
)

// +kubebuilder:object:root=true
// +kubebuilder:subresource:status
// +kubebuilder:resource:scope=Cluster,shortName=rp
// +kubebuilder:printcolumn:name="Source",type=string,JSONPath=`.spec.sourcePoolName`
// +kubebuilder:printcolumn:name="Dest",type=string,JSONPath=`.spec.destinationNFSServer`
// +kubebuilder:printcolumn:name="Schedule",type=string,JSONPath=`.spec.schedule`
// +kubebuilder:printcolumn:name="Phase",type=string,JSONPath=`.status.phase`
// +kubebuilder:printcolumn:name="Last Sync",type=date,JSONPath=`.status.lastSyncTime`

// ReplicationPolicy defines a replication relationship between a source pool
// and a destination NFS server for cross-region disaster recovery.
type ReplicationPolicy struct {
    metav1.TypeMeta   `json:",inline"`
    metav1.ObjectMeta `json:"metadata,omitempty"`

    Spec   ReplicationPolicySpec   `json:"spec,omitempty"`
    Status ReplicationPolicyStatus `json:"status,omitempty"`
}

// ReplicationPolicySpec defines the desired state of a replication policy.
type ReplicationPolicySpec struct {
    // SourcePoolName is the name of the FileSharePool CR on this cluster to replicate from.
    // +kubebuilder:validation:Required
    SourcePoolName string `json:"sourcePoolName"`

    // DestinationNFSServer is the NFS mount target IP of the destination pool,
    // reachable over Transit Gateway or VPN.
    // Required for direct NFS mode; omit when using driver-to-driver mode (DestinationEndpoint).
    // +optional
    DestinationNFSServer string `json:"destinationNFSServer,omitempty"`

    // DestinationExportPath is the NFS export path on the destination server.
    // For VPC access-mode shares, this differentiates shares under a shared FQDN.
    // Defaults to "/" if not specified.
    // +kubebuilder:default="/"
    // +optional
    DestinationExportPath string `json:"destinationExportPath,omitempty"`

    // DestinationBasePath is the base path on the destination NFS server
    // where replicated SubVolume directories are written (e.g., "/pvcs").
    // +kubebuilder:validation:Required
    DestinationBasePath string `json:"destinationBasePath"`

    // Schedule is a Go duration string controlling replication frequency.
    // Examples: "15m" (every 15 minutes), "1h" (hourly), "6h" (every 6 hours).
    // Parsed as time.Duration.
    // +kubebuilder:validation:Required
    Schedule string `json:"schedule"`

    // SubVolumeSelector selects which SubVolumes to replicate.
    // If nil, ALL SubVolumes in the source pool are replicated.
    // +optional
    SubVolumeSelector *metav1.LabelSelector `json:"subVolumeSelector,omitempty"`

    // MaxRetries is the number of consecutive failures before the policy is paused.
    // +kubebuilder:validation:Minimum=0
    // +kubebuilder:default=3
    MaxRetries int32 `json:"maxRetries"`

    // IncrementalSync enables rsync-based incremental replication instead of full copy.
    // When true (default), only changed files are transferred. Applies to direct NFS mode only;
    // receiver mode (destinationEndpoint) uploads the whole folder each cycle.
    // +kubebuilder:default=true
    // +optional
    IncrementalSync *bool `json:"incrementalSync,omitempty"`

    // BandwidthLimitMbps caps rsync transfer rate to avoid saturating
    // the cross-region link. 0 = unlimited.
    // +kubebuilder:validation:Minimum=0
    // +kubebuilder:default=0
    // +optional
    BandwidthLimitMbps int32 `json:"bandwidthLimitMbps"`

    // MaxParallelSyncs controls how many SubVolumes are rsynced concurrently.
    // Higher values reduce total sync time but increase network and CPU load.
    // The controller uses a semaphore-gated worker pool internally.
    // +kubebuilder:validation:Minimum=1
    // +kubebuilder:default=1
    // +optional
    MaxParallelSyncs int32 `json:"maxParallelSyncs"`

    // RsyncOptions allows passing extra rsync flags to customize transfer behavior.
    // These are appended to the default flags ["-a", "--delete", "--partial", "--timeout=300"].
    // Security: --daemon, --server, --rsh, and --rsync-path flags are blocked by validation.
    // Each entry must be one plain flag (for example --compress or --bwlimit=100): no spaces, quotes or shell characters.
    // Only applies to direct NFS mode (not driver-to-driver mode).
    // +optional
    RsyncOptions []string `json:"rsyncOptions,omitempty"`

    // VMCopySpeedLimitMBps is the highest speed, in megabytes per second, of
    // QEMU's copy of each disk of a running VM; unset or 0 means none. With
    // VMCopyAdaptive false it is the fixed speed (0 no limit, unset 20). The
    // copy also counts empty disk space. See "Running VM disks" below.
    // +kubebuilder:validation:Minimum=0
    // +optional
    VMCopySpeedLimitMBps *int32 `json:"vmCopySpeedLimitMBps,omitempty"`

    // VMCopyAdaptive makes the copy start at 15 MB/s for each disk, speed up while
    // the share the VM reads is quiet, and slow down when its average latency
    // passes VMCopyMaxLatencyMs. Default true. It needs the node agents' metrics;
    // without them the copy runs at the fixed speed.
    // +optional
    VMCopyAdaptive *bool `json:"vmCopyAdaptive,omitempty"`

    // VMCopyMaxLatencyMs is the share latency, in milliseconds, above which an
    // adaptive copy slows down. Default 15.
    // +kubebuilder:validation:Minimum=1
    // +kubebuilder:validation:Maximum=20
    // +optional
    VMCopyMaxLatencyMs *int32 `json:"vmCopyMaxLatencyMs,omitempty"`

    // RestorePointKeepHours is how long the destination keeps the restore
    // points of running VM disks. See "Running VM disks" below.
    // +kubebuilder:validation:Minimum=1
    // +kubebuilder:default=24
    // +optional
    RestorePointKeepHours *int32 `json:"restorePointKeepHours,omitempty"`

    // MomentKeepHours keeps earlier moments of volumes that are not VM disks,
    // as folders of hard links (in .moments next to the destination). A file that
    // did not change takes no extra space. A moment older than this many hours
    // is removed after each sync. Unset or 0 keeps none. Needs rsync, even when
    // IncrementalSync is false. BackupPolicy sets this.
    // +kubebuilder:validation:Minimum=0
    // +optional
    MomentKeepHours *int32 `json:"momentKeepHours,omitempty"`

    // DestinationEndpoint is the HTTPS URL of the replication receiver service
    // on the destination cluster (e.g., "https://repl-receiver.apps.cluster.example.com").
    // When set, the controller uses driver-to-driver mode instead of direct NFS.
    // +optional
    DestinationEndpoint string `json:"destinationEndpoint,omitempty"`

    // DestinationAuthSecretRef is the name of a Secret in kube-system containing
    // a "token" key with the bearer token for authenticating to the receiver.
    // Required when DestinationEndpoint is set.
    // +optional
    DestinationAuthSecretRef string `json:"destinationAuthSecretRef,omitempty"`

    // DestinationCACertSecretRef is the name of a Secret in kube-system containing
    // a "ca.crt" key with the CA certificate for verifying the receiver's TLS cert.
    // Required when the receiver uses a self-signed certificate.
    // +optional
    DestinationCACertSecretRef string `json:"destinationCACertSecretRef,omitempty"`

    // PreSyncHooks are hooks executed before each replication sync cycle.
    // +optional
    PreSyncHooks []Hook `json:"preSyncHooks,omitempty"`

    // PostSyncHooks are hooks executed after each replication sync cycle.
    // +optional
    PostSyncHooks []Hook `json:"postSyncHooks,omitempty"`
}

// ReplicationPolicyStatus describes the observed state of a replication policy.
type ReplicationPolicyStatus struct {
    // Phase is the overall replication state.
    // +kubebuilder:validation:Enum=Active;Paused;Failed
    Phase string `json:"phase,omitempty"`

    // LastSyncTime is when the last successful replication cycle completed.
    // +optional
    LastSyncTime *metav1.Time `json:"lastSyncTime,omitempty"`

    // LastSyncDuration is how long the last successful sync took, as a Go duration string.
    // +optional
    LastSyncDuration string `json:"lastSyncDuration,omitempty"`

    // SubVolumeStatuses tracks per-SubVolume replication state.
    // +optional
    SubVolumeStatuses []SubVolumeReplicationStatus `json:"subVolumeStatuses,omitempty"`

    // VMs lists each running VM: its disks, the copy moment and consistency
    // (the oldest copy among the disks), and CommonMoments, the moments ALL
    // its disks can show (the copy moment and the restore points every disk
    // has), newest first. Rewinding disks to different moments would give the
    // guest a mix of two times, so a recovery must use one of these. This is
    // the source cluster's view of the destination and can be a few minutes
    // old; a Failover plan is the exact view.
    // +optional
    VMs []VMReplicationStatus `json:"vms,omitempty"`

    // ConsecutiveFailures counts sequential failed replication cycles.
    // Resets to 0 on success.
    ConsecutiveFailures int32 `json:"consecutiveFailures"`

    // LastError is the error message from the most recent failure.
    // +optional
    LastError string `json:"lastError,omitempty"`

    // Conditions holds ReceiverReachable for a receiver-mode policy (see below).
    // +optional
    Conditions []metav1.Condition `json:"conditions,omitempty"`
}

// SubVolumeReplicationStatus tracks the replication state of a single SubVolume.
type SubVolumeReplicationStatus struct {
    // SubVolumeName is the SubVolume CR name.
    SubVolumeName string `json:"subVolumeName"`

    // LastSyncTime for this specific SubVolume.
    // +optional
    LastSyncTime *metav1.Time `json:"lastSyncTime,omitempty"`

    // BytesSynced in the last sync for this SubVolume.
    // +optional
    BytesSynced *int64 `json:"bytesSynced,omitempty"`

    // LastError recorded for this SubVolume's last sync attempt.
    // +optional
    LastError string `json:"lastError,omitempty"`

    // CopyMoment is the moment the last good copy of a running VM's disk shows.
    // All disks of the VM in this policy show the same moment.
    // +optional
    CopyMoment *metav1.Time `json:"copyMoment,omitempty"`

    // Consistency of the last good copy of a running VM's disk:
    // FileSystemConsistent or CrashConsistent.
    // +optional
    Consistency string `json:"consistency,omitempty"`

    // ConsistencyReason says why a copy is only crash consistent.
    // +optional
    ConsistencyReason string `json:"consistencyReason,omitempty"`

    // VMChangeList is the change list (QEMU dirty bitmap) of the last good
    // copy of a running VM's disk; the next copy holds only blocks changed
    // since then. Empty means the next copy is full.
    // +optional
    VMChangeList string `json:"vmChangeList,omitempty"`

    // RestorePoints is how many earlier copies the destination keeps for a
    // running VM's disk, and OldestRestorePoint the moment of the oldest.
    // +optional
    RestorePoints int32 `json:"restorePoints,omitempty"`
    // +optional
    OldestRestorePoint *metav1.Time `json:"oldestRestorePoint,omitempty"`

    // RestorePointMoments lists those restore points, oldest first.
    // +optional
    RestorePointMoments []metav1.Time `json:"restorePointMoments,omitempty"`

    // VMName is "namespace/name" of the VM that owns the disk.
    // +optional
    VMName string `json:"vmName,omitempty"`

    // VMCopy is the state of an unfinished running VM disk copy: copy ID,
    // phase (Copying or Sending), VM pod name and UID, VMI name, pod volume
    // name, disk index, staging file name, moment, freeze result, and the
    // change lists it started and read.
    // +optional
    VMCopy *VMCopyState `json:"vmCopy,omitempty"`
}

VMCopyState (api/v1alpha1/replicationpolicy_types.go) holds the state of one unfinished running VM disk copy:

// VMCopyState is the state of an unfinished copy of a running VM's disk.
type VMCopyState struct {
    // ID names the copy. It is the same for all disks of one VM copy.
    ID string `json:"id"`

    // Phase is Copying while QEMU writes the staging file, and Sending while
    // a Job applies it at the destination.
    // +kubebuilder:validation:Enum=Copying;Sending
    Phase string `json:"phase"`

    // PodNamespace is the namespace of the VM pod. A snapshot copy sets it so the
    // copy can be watched and cancelled without its source volume.
    // +optional
    PodNamespace string `json:"podNamespace,omitempty"`

    // PodName and PodUID identify the virt-launcher pod. If the pod changes,
    // the VM restarted or moved and QEMU no longer has the copy.
    PodName string `json:"podName"`
    PodUID  string `json:"podUID"`

    // VMIName is the VirtualMachineInstance name.
    VMIName string `json:"vmiName"`

    // Volume is the pod volume name of this disk, and DiskIndex its place in
    // the copy.
    Volume    string `json:"volume"`
    DiskIndex int32  `json:"diskIndex"`

    // StagingFile is the staging file name in the volume's root directory.
    StagingFile string `json:"stagingFile"`

    // Moment is the moment the copy shows.
    Moment metav1.Time `json:"moment"`

    // FileSystemConsistent is true if the guest was frozen for the copy.
    FileSystemConsistent bool `json:"fileSystemConsistent"`

    // FreezeError is the freeze error, if the freeze failed.
    // +optional
    FreezeError string `json:"freezeError,omitempty"`
}

docs.title: Running VM disks
docs.text:
In direct NFS mode, the controller copies the disks of a running VM without stopping it. It finds the VM from the virt-launcher pod that mounts the claim. On a scheduled cycle it freezes the guest file systems (KubeVirt's virt-freezer, with a 30 s automatic thaw), makes QEMU copy all of the VM's disks in the policy at one moment into sparse staging files in each volume, and thaws the guest. In the same step QEMU starts a change list for each disk. The next copy holds only the blocks changed since the last good copy; after a VM restart or move the lists are gone and the copy is full. Between scheduled cycles the controller checks the copy on every controller tick. When QEMU finishes, a Job per disk applies the copy to the destination disk.img: it first saves the old contents of every block it will change in an undo file in .repl-undo/ next to the disk, then writes the new blocks. A copy that stops half way is rolled back from its undo file by the next Job. The undo files are restore points, kept for restorePointKeepHours. Only blocks whose contents differ are written and saved. The lastSyncTime of a VM disk is the moment the copy shows, not the time the copy finished.

  • If a live migration of the VM is requested, the controller cancels the copy, because QEMU cannot migrate during a copy. The next cycle starts a new copy.
  • If the VM restarts or moves during a copy, the copy is lost and the next cycle starts a new one.
  • If the guest cannot freeze (no guest agent, or a freeze error), the copy is crash consistent, and consistency and consistencyReason say so.
  • A failed or skipped VM disk copy is reported in the volume's lastError and counted in the policy's lastError. It does not count as a failed cycle, so it does not pause the policy.
  • In receiver mode (destinationEndpoint set) the same copy is made, and a send-vm-disk Job per disk sends it to the receiver instead of writing to an NFS destination. For a full copy the Job first sends a hash of each 64 KiB chunk, and the receiver answers which chunks differ from its own disk, so only those cross the network. The receiver applies the copy with the same undo-file method, at the destination. If the destination disk does not show the moment the change copy starts from, the Job reports it, the status lastError says so, and the next copy is a full copy.
  • Hot-plugged disks are skipped.
  • Red Hat does not support the QEMU commands this uses. See docs/specs/2026-10-20-vm-safe-replication.md.

docs.title: Example ReplicationPolicy CR
docs.text:
apiVersion: storage.ibmcloud.io/v1alpha1
kind: ReplicationPolicy
metadata:
  name: dr-us-south-to-us-east
spec:
  sourcePoolName: general-purpose
  destinationNFSServer: "10.241.5.10"                  # DR site NFS IP via Transit Gateway
  destinationBasePath: /pvcs
  schedule: "15m"                                        # Replicate every 15 minutes
  maxRetries: 3
  bandwidthLimitMbps: 500                                # Cap at 500 Mbps
  maxParallelSyncs: 4                                    # Sync 4 SubVolumes concurrently
  rsyncOptions: ["--compress", "--checksum"]             # Extra rsync flags
  subVolumeSelector:                                     # Only replicate labeled SubVolumes
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/part-of: critical-app
status:
  phase: Active
  lastSyncTime: "2026-02-15T12:15:00Z"
  lastSyncDuration: "2m30s"
  consecutiveFailures: 0
  subVolumeStatuses:
    - subVolumeName: pvc-a1b2c3d4-5678-90ab-cdef-1234567890ab
      lastSyncTime: "2026-02-15T12:15:00Z"
      bytesSynced: 104857600
    - subVolumeName: pvc-b2c3d4e5-6789-01bc-def0-234567890abc
      lastSyncTime: "2026-02-15T12:14:55Z"
      bytesSynced: 52428800

docs.title: Example ReplicationPolicy CR Replicating All SubVolumes
docs.text:
apiVersion: storage.ibmcloud.io/v1alpha1
kind: ReplicationPolicy
metadata:
  name: dr-full-pool-replication
spec:
  sourcePoolName: general-purpose
  destinationNFSServer: "10.241.5.10"
  destinationBasePath: /pvcs
  schedule: "1h"                                         # Replicate hourly
  maxRetries: 5
  # subVolumeSelector omitted — all SubVolumes in the pool are replicated

docs.title: Example ReplicationPolicy CR Using Driver-to-Driver Mode
docs.text:
Driver-to-driver mode streams data over HTTPS to a receiver service on the destination cluster, eliminating the need for direct NFS connectivity between regions.

apiVersion: storage.ibmcloud.io/v1alpha1
kind: ReplicationPolicy
metadata:
  name: dr-driver-to-driver
spec:
  sourcePoolName: general-purpose
  destinationEndpoint: "https://repl-receiver-kube-system.apps.dr-cluster.example.com"
  destinationAuthSecretRef: replication-auth          # Secret in kube-system with "token" key
  destinationBasePath: /pvcs
  schedule: "2m"
  maxRetries: 3
  maxParallelSyncs: 2

docs.title: ReplicationPolicy Lifecycle
docs.text:
1. Active: The policy is operating normally. Replication cycles run on the configured schedule.
  2. Paused: Replication has been paused — either manually via the storage.ibmcloud.io/paused=true annotation, or automatically after maxRetries consecutive failures. Remove the annotation to resume.
  3. Failed: A permanent failure has occurred (e.g., destination unreachable after all retries).

docs.title: Pause/Resume via Annotation
docs.text:
# Pause replication (controller stops creating new sync Jobs)
kubectl annotate replicationpolicy <name> storage.ibmcloud.io/paused=true

# Resume replication (controller resumes sync cycles)
kubectl annotate replicationpolicy <name> storage.ibmcloud.io/paused-

docs.title: Replication Behavior
docs.text:
• Each replication cycle iterates over all SubVolumes matching the subVolumeSelector (or all SubVolumes in the pool if no selector is set).
  • For each SubVolume in direct NFS mode, an incremental rsync copies changed files from the source subdirectory to the destination NFS server at destinationBasePath/<subPath>. In receiver mode, the whole subdirectory is tarred and uploaded to the receiver each cycle.
  • consecutiveFailures increments on each failed cycle and resets to 0 on success. When it reaches maxRetries, the policy transitions to Paused.
  • conditions has ReceiverReachable for a policy with destinationEndpoint (driver-to-driver mode); direct-NFS policies have none. The controller reads the token and CA Secrets in kube-system, calls the receiver's /api/v1/health and /api/v1/auth-check, and records True (reason Reachable) or False with one reason and a plain message: CertificateNotTrusted, TokenRefused, StorageNotReachable, ReceiverTooOld, CannotConnect, TimedOut, SecretMissing or BadInput. It checks when it first sees the policy and then once per schedule. A False result does not pause or stop replication; it explains why a sync fails.
  • Per-SubVolume status in subVolumeStatuses allows operators to identify which volumes are failing independently.

docs.title: Failover
docs.text: Cluster-scoped resource (short name fo). Asks the driver on the destination (DR) cluster to read a replicated copy and plan, or carry out, a failover. A controller (on the leader) starts a Job in the driver's namespace that mounts the destination claim and runs --mode=failover, which runs the same code as kubectl failover (pkg/failover). The Job writes its result as JSON in its termination message (plain JSON, or gz: plus base64 gzip if larger than 3800 bytes), and the controller copies it into status. Go types: api/v1alpha1/failover_types.go.

docs.title: Spec
docs.text:
Field Type Meaning source string Destination claim to read, in the driver's namespace. Empty means the Helm value replicationReceiver.pvcName action Plan | Execute Required. Plan reads and reports; Execute also makes the SubVolume, PV and PVC objects rewindTo time The newest moment at or before it is used for each running VM vms []string Only these running VMs, each as namespace/name. Empty (the default) means every VM on the copy and every volume that is not a VM disk, as before. With a list, all disks of a chosen VM come together, and nothing else is planned or failed over: no other VM and no plain volume. A name that is not a running VM on the copy fails the Plan and lists the VMs that are. The order and repeats do not matter namespace string Namespace of the PVCs that are made (Execute) force bool Go on although a copy may still be applied; an unfinished copy is rolled back first drPool string FileSharePool the new SubVolumes belong to. Required for Execute basePath string The folder of the claim that holds the copies: the ReplicationPolicy's destinationBasePath. The copies are read from <claim>/<basePath>/pvcs. Empty means / (the claim's root). An absolute path of letters, digits, ., _, - and /, without ... An Execute needs a Plan with the same basePath drShareIP, drExportPath string NFS server and export of the claim's folder (without basePath, which is added). Empty means they are read from the claim's volume: an NFS volume (its server and path), or a volume of this driver (the server attribute, and the share attribute plus the subDir attribute). Set them to override

The spec cannot change after creation.

A Plan fails (it is not an empty Planned) if the claim has no <basePath>/pvcs folder, or the folder holds no replicated volume. The message says what was looked for and where. If copies exist under another folder of the claim, it names the basePath to use.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Field Meaning phase Planning, Planned, Executing, Done or Failed message Why it failed source The claim that was read startedAt, finishedAt Bounds of the run rpo Age of the oldest moment that will be shown vms[] Each running VM: name (namespace/name), moment it will show, moments (all moments its disks can show, newest first) and disks[] (subVolume, rewind: false is "in place", true copies the whole disk) volumes[] Every volume that is failed over, with its claim, size, folder (subPath, the new folder for a rewound disk), owner and policy momentsTruncated The lists of moments were cut to fit the termination message (newest kept) createdPVCs[] The PVCs an Execute made

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
apiVersion: storage.ibmcloud.io/v1alpha1
kind: Failover
metadata:
  name: plan-1
spec:
  action: Plan
---
apiVersion: storage.ibmcloud.io/v1alpha1
kind: Failover
metadata:
  name: go-1
spec:
  action: Execute
  drPool: dr-production
  rewindTo: "2026-10-21T10:30:00Z"   # same as the Plan
---
# Fail over one VM. The Plan and the Execute name the same VMs.
apiVersion: storage.ibmcloud.io/v1alpha1
kind: Failover
metadata:
  name: plan-web
spec:
  action: Plan
  vms: ["apps/web"]

docs.title: Safety
docs.text:
• An Execute is refused (by the webhook, and again by the controller) unless a Plan with the same source, rewindTo and vms (compared as sets) is Planned and finished in the last 15 minutes.
  • The Job gets the confirmed plan (the moment of each VM and the volume names). If the share now gives another plan, the Job stops before it rewinds or changes anything, and the Failover is Failed with the difference.
  • With vms set, the Job reads and checks only the chosen VMs. A copy that is still being applied to another VM, or another VM with no moment at or before rewindTo, does not block the chosen ones. The status, the created objects and the "already failed over" check cover only the chosen VMs.
  • A volume that has a failed-over SubVolume (label storage.ibmcloud.io/failover-source) on this cluster is refused, so a VM is not failed over twice.
  • The Job runs as user 107, because that user owns the replicated disks. A rewind never changes the latest disk.
  • RBAC: the ClusterRole <release>-failover-admin gives access to failovers. It is bound to nobody.

docs.title: StorageClass Parameters
docs.text:
Auto-creation: When a FileSharePool reaches Ready, the controller automatically creates a matching StorageClass named after the pool (e.g., pool general-purpose gets StorageClass general-purpose). For tiered pools, one StorageClass per tier is created (e.g., general-purpose-standard, general-purpose-premium). Auto-created StorageClasses have an OwnerReference to the pool and are garbage-collected when the pool is deleted.

To opt out, add the annotation storage.ibmcloud.io/skip-storageclass: "true" to the FileSharePool before creating it.

The CSI driver reads these from the StorageClass parameters map:

Parameter Required Default Description pool Yes — Name of the FileSharePool CR tier No — Tier name within a tiered pool (required for tiered pools) uid No Pool default Unix UID for the subdirectory gid No Pool default Unix GID for the subdirectory permissions No Pool default Unix permissions (e.g., "0755")

Example auto-created StorageClass (for a pool named general-purpose): 

apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: general-purpose
  labels:
    storage.ibmcloud.io/managed-by: ibm-vpc-file-pool-csi
    storage.ibmcloud.io/pool: general-purpose
  ownerReferences:
    - apiVersion: storage.ibmcloud.io/v1alpha1
      kind: FileSharePool
      name: general-purpose
      uid: <pool-uid>
provisioner: vpc-file-pool.csi.ibm.io
parameters:
  pool: general-purpose
reclaimPolicy: Delete
volumeBindingMode: Immediate
allowVolumeExpansion: true
mountOptions:
  - nfsvers=4.1
  - soft
  - timeo=600
  - retrans=3

Example manual StorageClass (if opting out of auto-creation): 

apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: ibm-vpc-file-pool
provisioner: vpc-file-pool.csi.ibm.io
parameters:
  pool: general-purpose
  uid: "1000"
  gid: "1000"
  permissions: "0755"
reclaimPolicy: Delete
volumeBindingMode: Immediate
allowVolumeExpansion: true
mountOptions:
  - nfsvers=4.1
  - soft
  - timeo=600
  - retrans=3

docs.title: CRD Generation
docs.text:
After modifying types, regenerate:

# Install controller-gen if not present
go install sigs.k8s.io/controller-tools/cmd/controller-gen@latest

# Generate CRD YAML manifests
controller-gen crd paths="./api/..." output:crd:dir=config/crd

# Generate deep copy methods
controller-gen object paths="./api/..."

The generated CRD YAMLs go into config/crd/ and are applied to the cluster with kubectl apply -f config/crd/.

docs.title: Cross-Region Disaster Recovery (Phase 4d)
docs.text:
Design document for cross-region replication of pooled file share data.

Status: Implemented (v0.5.0) Depends on: Phase 4a (Snapshots), cross-region VPC connectivity Last updated: 2026-02-17

Implementation note: The implementation simplifies several aspects of this design: - Direct NFS mode uses SyncDir (rsync-based incremental) by default, with CopyDir (full copy) as fallback when incrementalSync is disabled. Receiver mode (destinationEndpoint) does not use rsync: it tars and uploads the whole folder each cycle - Uses time.Duration schedule intervals instead of cron expressions - Destination is specified via DestinationNFSServer IP rather than a pool reference with share mappings - Pre/post-sync lifecycle hooks are implemented (Phase 5) — supports both exec (pod command) and HTTP hook types with configurable abort/continue-on-error policies

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Phase 4d adds optional cross-region disaster recovery for FileSharePool volumes. The goal is to allow cluster operators to replicate SubVolume data from a source pool in one IBM Cloud region to a destination pool in another region, so that workloads can be restarted in the DR region with a recent copy of their data.

This feature is not a general-purpose replication engine. It is designed for a narrow set of workloads where file-level consistency is sufficient and where the application can tolerate a non-zero Recovery Point Objective (RPO). It is explicitly unsuitable for workloads that require crash consistency, cross-file transactional guarantees, or intra-file point-in-time consistency.

docs.title: Platform Constraints
docs.text: This section documents what the IBM VPC platform does and does not provide. These constraints are fundamental and cannot be worked around at the driver level.

docs.title: What IBM VPC File Shares Do NOT Provide
docs.text: Capability Status Impact Native cross-region replication Not available No async/sync mirror, no replica shares across regions. All replication must be built at the application layer. Share-level snapshots Available, not used The VPC API can snapshot a whole file share, but not for shares in vpc access mode. A pool share holds many volumes, so the driver does not use it: one volume could not be restored without touching the others. Directory-level snapshots Not available No way to atomically capture a subdirectory within a share. File-level snapshots Not available No copy-on-write or reflink support at the NFS protocol level. Change tracking / changelog Not available No journal, delta stream, or inotify-equivalent at the share level. Change detection requires full directory traversal. Cross-region share access Not available A file share in us-south cannot have mount targets in us-east. Shares are region-local.

docs.title: What IBM VPC File Shares DO Provide
docs.text: Capability Details NFS v4.1 Standard protocol with close-to-open cache consistency Cross-zone mount targets Shares in us-south-1 can have mount targets in us-south-2 and us-south-3 (same region, already implemented in Phase 3d) Encryption at rest Provider-managed or customer-managed keys Encryption in transit NFS over Kerberos (sec=krb5p)

docs.title: Network Connectivity Between Regions
docs.text:
Cross-region replication requires private network connectivity between regions. IBM Cloud provides:

  • Transit Gateway -- connects VPCs across regions over IBM's private backbone. This is the recommended path.
  • VPN Gateway -- IPsec tunnels between regions. Lower throughput, higher latency.
  • Public internet -- not recommended (security, cost, unreliable bandwidth).

The replication controller does not provision network connectivity. Transit Gateway or equivalent must be configured by the cluster operator as a prerequisite.

docs.title: Consistency Guarantees
docs.text: This is the most important section of this document. Read it carefully before deciding whether Phase 4d is appropriate for a given workload.

docs.title: What We CAN Guarantee
docs.text:
File-level consistency: Each individual file in the replicated copy is internally consistent. When NFS closes a file, the server flushes all pending writes. The replication tool (rsync) reads files after they are closed, so each file it copies reflects a complete write. If a 50 MB file was being written, rsync copies either the old version or the new version -- never a half-written version.

This guarantee comes from NFS close-to-open semantics: when a client closes a file, all data is flushed to the server. When another client (or rsync on the same client) opens the file, it sees all data that was flushed at the previous close.

docs.title: What We CANNOT Guarantee
docs.text:
Cross-file consistency: If an application writes to files A and B as part of a logical transaction, the replicated copy may contain the new version of A and the old version of B (or vice versa). There is no mechanism to capture a consistent snapshot across multiple files simultaneously.

Timeline on source:
  T1: Write file A (new)
  T2: rsync starts, copies A (new)
  T3: Write file B (new)    ← happens DURING rsync
  T4: rsync copies B (old)  ← rsync read B before T3 completed

Result on destination:
  A = new (T1)
  B = old (pre-T3)
  ← Cross-file inconsistency

Crash consistency: If the source application crashes or the node fails during a replication cycle, the destination may have a mix of pre-crash and during-crash file states. There is no rollback or atomic commit for the replication operation.

Intra-file consistency for active writers: If a file is being actively written (not yet closed) during the rsync window, the replicated copy may contain partial writes. This is an NFS protocol-level limitation -- NFS does not provide read isolation for files with open writers on other clients. rsync on the same node as the writer is somewhat better (close-to-open within the same client), but concurrent writes to the same file from different pods on the same node can still produce partial reads.

Application-level consistency: The replication engine has no knowledge of application semantics. It copies files. If an application requires that config.json and data.bin are updated atomically, replication cannot enforce this.

docs.title: Consistency Summary Table
docs.text: Guarantee Provided? Notes Each file internally consistent YES NFS close-to-open; rsync reads closed files Cross-file atomic consistency NO No multi-file snapshot Crash consistency NO No journal, no atomic capture Application consistency ONLY with quiesce hooks Application must freeze I/O before rsync Point-in-time recovery NO Each rsync cycle produces a "fuzzy" copy

docs.title: Unsupported Workload Types
docs.text: The following workloads MUST NOT be copied with rsync. A file copy of them produces corrupted or unusable replicas in the DR region. The controller never copies a running VM's disk with rsync: it uses a QEMU copy instead, as the VM section below describes.

docs.title: VM Boot and Data Disks (qcow2, vmdk, raw)
docs.text:
Why it fails: A VM performs scattered random writes within a single disk image file (disk.img). Even though rsync copies files, the problem is intra-file inconsistency during active VM operation. The VM writes block 1000 at T1, block 50000 at T2, block 3000 at T3 -- all within the same file. rsync reads this file while the VM is writing, producing a copy where some blocks are from T1, others from T2, others from T3. The result is a disk image with a structurally broken filesystem inside the VM.

The ext4 or xfs journal inside the VM is inconsistent. The VM will not boot, or it boots with filesystem corruption.

This is NOT a file-level consistency problem (rsync is reading one file). It is an intra-file consistency problem: the file's internal structure (filesystem metadata, journal, block allocation tables) requires all blocks to be from the same point in time, and rsync cannot provide that for a file being actively mutated by a VM.

What the controller does: in direct NFS mode, it copies a running VM's disks with QEMU, all at one moment, and never with rsync. The details are in CRD-SPEC.md, "Running VM disks". In receiver mode it does the same, and the receiver at the destination applies each copy, so each changed block crosses the network once. Hot-plugged disks are skipped, as described next.

Skipped volumes: it never copies a volume that a running or starting VM uses with rsync. Before each copy it looks for a KubeVirt pod (kubevirt.io=virt-launcher or kubevirt.io=hotplug-disk) in the claim's namespace that mounts the claim. If it finds one, it skips the volume and sets the volume's status error to skipped: in use by running VM <namespace>/<pod>; .... The policy's lastError counts the skipped volumes. A skipped volume does not count as a failed cycle, so it does not pause the policy for the other volumes. If a VM starts while a copy runs, the controller does not record that copy as a sync. If the controller cannot list the pods, it does not copy the volume. Volumes of stopped VMs are copied as before; rsync leaves out any staging files left by an earlier VM copy.

What to use instead: the QEMU copy that the controller makes of a running VM (above). Its status says FileSystemConsistent or CrashConsistent. IBM Cloud VPC block storage snapshots and replication are another option for VM workloads.

docs.title: Databases with Write-Ahead Logs
docs.text:
Why it fails: Databases like PostgreSQL, MySQL, and etcd maintain a write-ahead log (WAL) and data files that must be consistent with each other. The WAL says "transaction X wrote page Y" -- if the replica has the WAL entry but not the updated page (or vice versa), the database is corrupted.

Source database files:
  data/base/16384/1234   ← table data file
  data/pg_wal/000000010000000000000001  ← WAL segment

rsync copies:
  1. WAL segment (contains record of writing page 42 in table 1234)
  2. Table data file (does NOT yet contain the page 42 write)

Destination: WAL references a write that isn't in the data file.
Recovery will fail or produce silent data corruption.

What to use instead: Database-native replication (PostgreSQL streaming replication, MySQL Group Replication, etcd learner nodes). These tools understand their own transaction semantics.

docs.title: Applications Requiring Cross-File Transactional Consistency
docs.text:
Any application that writes to multiple files as a logical unit and requires all-or-nothing semantics across those files. Examples:

  • Configuration management systems that write a config file and a version marker atomically
  • Batch processing pipelines where an output file and a completion marker must arrive together
  • ML training checkpoints that span multiple files (model weights + optimizer state + metadata)

What to use instead: Application-level replication with quiesce hooks (see Supported Workloads), or redesign to use a single file per transaction boundary.

docs.title: Supported Workload Types
docs.text: Phase 4d is designed for workloads where file-level consistency is sufficient and where a non-zero RPO (minutes to hours) is acceptable.

docs.title: Static Assets, Model Weights, Config Archives
docs.text:
Files that are written once and read many times. rsync produces a correct copy because the files are not being modified during replication.

Example: ML model serving
  /pvcs/pvc-model/
    model-v42.bin        ← 2 GB, written once by training pipeline
    tokenizer.json       ← written once
    config.yaml          ← written once

  rsync copies all three files. Each is complete and consistent.
  DR region can serve the model immediately.

docs.title: Log Aggregation and Cold Data
docs.text: Log files are append-only. rsync copies the current state of each log file. The replica may be slightly behind (missing the last few seconds of logs), but every log entry that is present is complete.

docs.title: Warm Standby for Apps with Native Replication
docs.text: Applications that already handle replication at the application layer (e.g., Kafka, Elasticsearch, CockroachDB) but want a filesystem-level warm standby for faster DR bootstrap. The replicated data is not authoritative -- it is a starting point that reduces recovery time.

docs.title: Workloads with Quiesce Hooks
docs.text:
Applications that can freeze I/O on command. The replication controller calls a pre-sync hook (e.g., exec into a pod, run fsfreeze or an application-specific flush command), then runs rsync, then calls a post-sync hook to resume I/O. This converts the "fuzzy" copy into an application-consistent copy at the cost of a brief I/O pause.

Replication cycle with quiesce:

  1. Controller calls pre-sync hook: "kubectl exec app-pod -- /scripts/flush-and-freeze.sh"
  2. Application flushes buffers, stops writing
  3. rsync runs (all files are quiesced, no concurrent writers)
  4. Controller calls post-sync hook: "kubectl exec app-pod -- /scripts/thaw.sh"
  5. Application resumes writing

  During step 3, every file is consistent AND cross-file consistency is achieved
  because no writes are happening. The I/O pause window = rsync duration.

docs.title: Design Principles
docs.text:
1. Replication runs outside the CSI hot path. The replication controller is a background goroutine in the controller pod. It never touches CreateVolume, DeleteVolume, or node mount operations.
  2. All state in CRDs. ReplicationPolicy CRs define what to replicate. Status fields track progress, RPO, and errors.
  3. Two replication modes. Direct NFS mode: rsync between NFS-mounted source and destination shares over Transit Gateway. Driver-to-driver mode: sync-client Jobs tar-stream data over HTTPS to a receiver service on the destination cluster — no cross-region NFS connectivity needed.
  4. Fail open. If replication fails, the source cluster is unaffected. Replication errors are surfaced as CRD status and Prometheus metrics, never as PVC failures.
  5. Per-SubVolume granularity. Each SubVolume (PVC subdirectory) is replicated independently. The operator chooses which SubVolumes to replicate via label selectors.

docs.title: Component Diagram
docs.text:
• Source cluster (Primary): the CSI Controller Pod holds the CSI Controller (CreateVolume, DeleteVolume, Pool Manager) and the Replication Controller (goroutine). For each ReplicationPolicy the Replication Controller lists the matching SubVolumes, creates Kubernetes Jobs per SubVolume, and updates the status on completion. It reads the FileSharePool, SubVolume and ReplicationPolicy CRs.
  • Jobs: in Direct NFS mode, an rsync Job (CentOS). In Driver-to-Driver mode, a sync-client Job (driver image, tar over HTTPS).
  • Destination cluster (DR): in Direct NFS mode, the destination NFS share (mounted); rsync goes over Transit Gateway or VPN. In Driver-to-Driver mode, the Replication Receiver service (extracts the tar, writes metadata); the data goes as an HTTPS PUT via an OpenShift Route.

docs.title: Replication Controller
docs.text:
The replication controller is a background goroutine in the CSI controller pod (with leader election) that:

  1. Polls ReplicationPolicy CRs every 30 seconds. A policy starts a cycle when its schedule is due. While a cycle runs, the controller looks at the policy on every poll, and it also watches the Jobs in the driver namespace, so the policy status changes within seconds after a copy Job ends (not at the next scheduled cycle). Pre-sync hooks run once, when the cycle starts; post-sync hooks run once, when it ends.
  2. For each policy, resolves the source FileSharePool and its SubVolumes (filtered by label selector).
  3. Determines the replication mode based on the policy spec:
  4. Direct NFS mode (destinationNFSServer set): Creates rsync Jobs that mount both source and destination NFS shares.
  5. Driver-to-driver mode (destinationEndpoint set): Creates sync-client Jobs that tar-stream source data to the HTTPS receiver on the destination cluster.
  6. On each replication cycle, creates Kubernetes Jobs (up to maxParallelSyncs concurrent) for each SubVolume.
  7. Records completion time, bytes transferred, and duration in the ReplicationPolicy status.
  8. Exposes Prometheus metrics for replication lag, RPO, transfer rate, and error counts.
  9. Supports pause/resume via the storage.ibmcloud.io/paused annotation.

The controller does NOT: - Create or delete VPC file shares (the destination pool must already exist). - Create or delete SubVolume CRs on the destination (the failover CLI handles this). - Interfere with the CSI controller or node agent in any way.

docs.title: TLS Configuration (Driver-to-Driver Mode)
docs.text:
When using driver-to-driver mode, the receiver service accepts HTTPS uploads from sync-client Jobs. TLS secures data in transit between clusters and authenticates the receiver endpoint.

Receiver TLS (destination cluster):

The receiver supports native TLS via cert-manager. Enable it in Helm values:

replicationReceiver:
  enabled: true
  pvcName: replication-receiver-data
  authSecretName: replication-auth
  tls:
    enabled: true                    # Enables HTTPS on the receiver
    additionalDNSNames: []           # Extra SANs (optional)
    certManager:
      issuerKind: Issuer             # Issuer or ClusterIssuer
      issuerName: ""                 # Empty = auto-create self-signed Issuer

When tls.enabled=true: - A self-signed cert-manager Issuer and Certificate are created in kube-system - The Certificate includes SANs for the Service FQDN and the OpenShift Route hostname - The OpenShift Route switches to termination: passthrough (TLS terminates at the receiver, not the router) - Health probes use HTTPS instead of HTTP

CA certificate verification (source cluster):

When the receiver uses a self-signed certificate, sync-client Jobs need the CA cert to verify the connection. Configure this on the ReplicationPolicy:

apiVersion: storage.ibmcloud.io/v1alpha1
kind: ReplicationPolicy
metadata:
  name: cross-region-dr
spec:
  sourcePoolName: production
  destinationEndpoint: "https://repl-receiver-kube-system.apps.dr-cluster.example.com"
  destinationAuthSecretRef: replication-auth-dr       # Bearer token Secret
  destinationCACertSecretRef: repl-receiver-ca        # CA cert Secret
  destinationBasePath: /pvcs
  schedule: "15m"

The destinationCACertSecretRef references a Secret in kube-system containing the CA certificate under the ca.crt key. Extract it from the destination cluster's cert-manager Certificate:

# On the destination cluster: extract the CA cert
kubectl get secret repl-receiver-tls -n kube-system \
  -o jsonpath='{.data.ca\.crt}' | base64 -d > ca.crt

# On the source cluster: create the CA cert Secret
kubectl create secret generic repl-receiver-ca \
  -n kube-system --from-file=ca.crt=ca.crt
