docs.title: Helm Upgrade (Recommended)
docs.text:
# 1. Update the chart repository (if using a remote repo)
helm repo update

# 2. Preview changes
helm diff upgrade ibm-vpc-file-pool-csi charts/ibm-vpc-file-pool-csi/ \
  --namespace kube-system \
  --values my-values.yaml

# 3. Apply the upgrade
helm upgrade ibm-vpc-file-pool-csi charts/ibm-vpc-file-pool-csi/ \
  --namespace kube-system \
  --values my-values.yaml \
  --timeout 5m

# 4. Watch rollout
kubectl rollout status deployment/ibm-vpc-file-pool-csi-controller -n kube-system
kubectl rollout status daemonset/ibm-vpc-file-pool-csi-node -n kube-system

docs.title: Raw Manifest Upgrade
docs.text:
# 1. Apply updated CRDs first (CRDs are not managed by kubectl apply on deployments)
kubectl apply -f config/crd/

# 2. Apply updated RBAC
kubectl apply -f config/rbac/

# 3. Apply updated deployments and daemonsets
kubectl apply -f config/controller/
kubectl apply -f config/node/

# 4. Watch rollout
kubectl rollout status deployment/ibm-vpc-file-pool-csi-controller -n kube-system
kubectl rollout status daemonset/ibm-vpc-file-pool-csi-node -n kube-system

docs.title: CRD Upgrade Procedures
docs.text: CRDs require special handling because Helm does not upgrade CRDs on helm upgrade (by design).

docs.title: Additive Schema Changes (Safe)
docs.text:
Most upgrades add new optional fields to existing CRDs. These are backward-compatible — existing CRs continue to work without modification. Apply the new CRDs before upgrading the controller:

kubectl apply -f config/crd/

docs.title: Breaking Schema Changes
docs.text: No versions to date have introduced breaking CRD schema changes. All field additions have been optional with backward-compatible defaults. If a future version requires a breaking change, it will be called out explicitly in the CHANGELOG and this guide will be updated with migration steps.

docs.title: Verifying CRD Updates
docs.text:
# Check CRD versions
kubectl get crd filesharepools.storage.ibmcloud.io -o jsonpath='{.spec.versions[*].name}'
kubectl get crd subvolumes.storage.ibmcloud.io -o jsonpath='{.spec.versions[*].name}'

# Verify new fields are present (example: check for ExportPath added in v0.9.0)
kubectl get crd filesharepools.storage.ibmcloud.io -o json | \
  python3 -c "import sys,json; schema=json.load(sys.stdin); print('exportPath' in str(schema))"

docs.title: Upgrading to v0.16.3 (from v0.16.2)
docs.text:
Changes: a new pool can no longer end with a share that has no mount target. A lost status save is saved again, and a share without a mount target switches to the same-named share that has one.

CRD changes: none.

Action required: upgrade with Helm (set image.tag and consolePlugin.image.tag to v0.16.3 if you pin them). To go back, run helm rollback.

docs.title: Upgrading to v0.16.2 (from v0.16.1)
docs.text:
Changes: a wrong COS key is named as the cause when browsing or restoring files from COS, instead of "COS could not be read".

CRD changes: none.

Action required: upgrade with Helm (set image.tag and consolePlugin.image.tag to v0.16.2 if you pin them). To go back, run helm rollback.

docs.title: Upgrading to v0.16.1 (from v0.16.0)
docs.text:
Changes: - Audit Events for backup browsing and file restore are recorded. In v0.16.0 the API server refused them. They are now written on the ConfigMap backup-gateway-info in the driver namespace, so only people who can read Events there see them. Each Event names the session or restore it is about. - The gateway address in backup-gateway-info is filled in on a first install, so kubectl backup no longer needs --gateway until a second upgrade. - The replication policy page shows the last error as an error alert.

CRD changes: none.

Action required: upgrade with Helm (set image.tag and consolePlugin.image.tag to v0.16.1 if you pin them). To go back, run helm rollback.

docs.title: Upgrading to v0.16.0 (from v0.15.3)
docs.text:
Changes: - Failover from the console. A new cluster-scoped resource Failover plans and runs a failover on the destination cluster (all VMs, or the VMs you name). The console has a Recovery page for it, and the replication policy page shows how each running VM can be recovered. Nothing is bound to the <release>-failover-admin role: bind it to the people who may fail over. - Browse and restore files from a backup. A new backup gateway (a Deployment, a Service and on OpenShift a Route) and kubectl backup ls / get / browse / restore-files. The console has a file browser, download and a restore dialog. A new resource BackupFileRestore runs the restore. Backups in COS can be browsed too (plain volumes only; VM disks inside backups are not covered yet). - A volume request that finds no room may create one share when autoExpand is on. The code did this before; the rule text now says so. - Fixes: failover works when the receiver's data claim is a claim the driver provisioned, and a failover Plan with no copies now fails with a clear message; the PoolBench backup event shows the copy speed; the console restore banner waits for the copy state.

CRD changes (additive): two new CRDs, Failover and BackupFileRestore; new fields on ReplicationPolicy status (vms), and source/fromCOS on BackupBrowse. Apply them first: kubectl apply --server-side --force-conflicts -f config/crd/.

New objects from the chart: a namespace ibm-vpc-file-pool-csi-browse (backupBrowse.namespace) for browse sessions, which allows root pods without capabilities; on OpenShift one SCC for it; the gateway Deployment, Service, Route and ConfigMap backup-gateway-info; ClusterRoles for the gateway, failover-admin, and a Role in the driver namespace that lets the controller create and delete the per-session Secrets for COS browsing. Both backupBrowse.enabled and backupGateway.enabled are on by default; turn them off to avoid these objects. A cluster that is not OpenShift needs backupGateway.tls.secretName.

Action required: 1. Apply the CRDs. 2. Upgrade with Helm. Set image.tag if you pin it. The browse and console plugin images change too (consolePlugin.image.tag, and the browse tag follows the driver tag unless set). 3. Bind <release>-failover-admin to the administrators who may fail over.

To go back, run helm rollback. Unused new CRDs stay.

docs.title: Upgrading to v0.15.3 (from v0.15.2)
docs.text:
Changes: - PoolBench: the backup event reports the copy speed. The PoolBench service can now read replication policies. Before, it read no speed and said nothing.

CRD changes: none. No chart value changes.

Action required: upgrade with Helm (the role is part of the chart). Set image.tag if you pin it. The console plugin image did not change.

To go back, run helm rollback.

docs.title: Upgrading to v0.15.2 (from v0.15.1)
docs.text:
Changes: - The controller role can watch pods, so the volume resizer sidecar stops logging "Failed to watch *v1.Pod" and stops restarting.

CRD changes: none. No chart value changes. The driver and console plugin images did not change.

Action required: upgrade with Helm (the role is part of the chart). Set image.tag if you pin it.

To go back, run helm rollback.

docs.title: Upgrading to v0.15.1 (from v0.15.0)
docs.text:
Changes: - A COS export of a backup no longer reads a disk that changes under it (issue #310). While the export of a volume runs, the next local backup of that volume waits; all disks of a running VM wait together. The volume's status says held: export to COS running. A hold ends with the export, or after 6 hours. - The adaptive copy speed now also changes the speed of the disks that still copy when another disk of the VM has finished (issue #313). - PoolBench: the backup event reports the copy speed and the latency of the VMs during the backup.

CRD changes (additive): new fields in the status of PoolBench events. The SubVolume gets a short-lived annotation storage.ibmcloud.io/export-hold while an export runs. No chart value changes.

Action required: 1. Apply the CRDs: kubectl apply --server-side --force-conflicts -f config/crd/. 2. Upgrade with Helm. Set image.tag if you pin it. The console plugin image did not change.

To go back, run helm rollback. The older driver ignores the annotation.

docs.title: Upgrading to v0.15.0 (from v0.14.3)
docs.text:
Changes: - Copies of running VM disks (replication, backup and snapshot copies) adapt their speed to the load on the share the VM reads. A copy starts at 15 MB/s, speeds up by 5 MB/s every 30 seconds while the share is quiet, and halves (never below 15 MB/s) when the average latency of the share passes vmCopyMaxLatencyMs (15 ms by default). - The fixed 20 MB/s default is gone for adaptive copies. vmCopySpeedLimitMBps is now the highest speed, and unset means there is no highest speed. If you rely on 20 MB/s as a ceiling, set vmCopySpeedLimitMBps: 20. To keep a fixed speed, set vmCopyAdaptive: false on the policy (or on the VolumeSnapshotClass). - PoolBench, a storage performance test in the console. It is off by default (poolBench.enabled).

CRD changes (additive): the new PoolBench resource, and vmCopyAdaptive and vmCopyMaxLatencyMs on BackupPolicy and ReplicationPolicy. vmCopySpeedLimitMBps no longer has a default of 20. The status of a replication volume shows the speed now in vmCopy.speedMBps.

New objects from the chart: a service account <release>-node-reader that can only read the node agents' /metrics; a Role for the controller (list endpoint slices, create a token of that one account); a ConfigMap <release>-node-ca that the OpenShift service CA fills in. On a cluster without the OpenShift service CA, copies stay at the fixed speed.

Action required: 1. Apply the CRDs: kubectl apply --server-side --force-conflicts -f config/crd/. 2. Upgrade with Helm. Set both image.tag and consolePlugin.image.tag if you pin image tags. No chart value changes are needed. 3. Check the controller log: a line "Cannot read the latency of the pool's shares" means the copies stay at their fixed speed, and the line says why.

To go back, run helm rollback. The older driver works with the new CRDs.

docs.title: Upgrading to v0.14.3 (from v0.14.2)
docs.text:
Changes: the node agent finishes the unmount of a volume whose share was already deleted. Before, such a volume stayed on the node, and kubelet repeated a failing unmount forever. Share metrics are no longer minutes late on a node with dead mounts. See CHANGELOG.md.

CRD changes: none.

Action required: 1. Upgrade with Helm. No CRD step, and no chart value changes. Set both image.tag and consolePlugin.image.tag if you pin image tags. 2. Nothing to clean by hand. After the upgrade, kubelet's next retries remove the leftover volumes of deleted shares from each node. Each one takes up to about 4 minutes. To check a node, count the folders under <kubelet dir>/plugins/kubernetes.io/csi/vpc-file-pool.csi.ibm.io/: only volumes in use stay.

docs.title: Upgrading to v0.14.2 (from v0.14.1)
docs.text:
Changes: the node agent /metrics endpoint no longer answers HTTP 500 when a node holds the same share twice, so share metrics and the alerts built on them work again on those nodes. The driver refuses CreateVolume on a backup policy's snapshot pool (FailedPrecondition, naming the policy), and the console leaves those pools out of its lists. The console clone banner follows the copy, a refused "Delete backups" dialog says "Close", and the clone and restore pages no longer call their own new claim a taken name. See CHANGELOG.md.

CRD changes: none.

Action required: 1. Upgrade with Helm. No CRD step, and no chart value changes. 2. Upgrade the driver and the console plugin image to v0.14.2 together. If you pin image tags, set both image.tag and consolePlugin.image.tag. 3. If a volume already sits on a backup policy's snapshot pool, it stays. Only new volumes on that pool are refused. Move the volume off the pool so the policy backs up again.

docs.title: Upgrading to v0.14.1 (from v0.14.0)
docs.text:
Changes: the console box on the Snapshots and Pools pages now shows how the driver takes VM disk snapshots: instant, copy, or unknown. Before, it read only the KubeVirt Sidecar gate and said "on" even when the driver was set to vmSnapshots.method=copy. The driver code is the same as v0.14.0.

CRD changes: none.

Action required: 1. Upgrade with Helm. No CRD step. 2. The chart now renders a ConfigMap ibm-vpc-file-pool-csi-settings (key vmSnapshotMethod, no secret) in the release namespace, and a Role and RoleBinding that let every signed-in user get that one ConfigMap by name. Nothing else in the namespace becomes readable. The console reads it. 3. Upgrade the console plugin image to v0.14.1 with the chart. A console plugin that is newer than the driver shows "unknown" until the driver is upgraded too.

docs.title: Upgrading to v0.14.0 (from v0.13.2)
docs.text:
Changes: shares use security group access mode; VM snapshots and replication use a QEMU copy of running VMs; golden images are imported by CDI; new console pages. See CHANGELOG.md for the full list.

CRD changes (additive): FileSharePool.spec.securityGroupIDs, new status fields on Snapshot (consistency, copyMoment) and ReplicationPolicy (restore points, copy moments), and ReplicationPolicy.spec.vmCopySpeedLimitMBps.

Action required: 1. Apply updated CRDs: kubectl apply -f config/crd/ 2. Upgrade with Helm. The controller ClusterRole gains permissions (DataVolumes, DataSources, KubeVirt migrations, the kubevirt-controller SCC, hyperconvergeds) and loses ImageStreams and RoleBindings. 3. Shares you made before this version in VPC access mode keep working until IBM ends support on 6 May 2027. New shares use security group access mode. The driver does not change an existing share. 4. If the Prometheus Operator API is present, the chart now creates a ServiceMonitor by default (metrics.serviceMonitor.enabled). 5. BREAKING: the controller metrics endpoint (:8080/metrics) is now HTTPS with a token login (PR #174). Anything that scraped it over plain HTTP must change to HTTPS with a bearer token. The node agent also serves metrics on port 9810 over HTTPS. 6. On OpenShift, alerts need user workload monitoring turned on (enableUserWorkload: true); without it no alert fires. The chart does not change that setting. The command is in docs/INSTALL.md. 7. The guides moved into docs/ (PR #184). README, CHANGELOG, CONTRIBUTING, CLAUDE.md and SKILL.md stay in the root. Update bookmarks; the console help links already point to docs/. A branch that edits a guide at its old place: run hack/follow-docs-move.sh after git merge origin/main. 8. Hardening (PRs #156, #105, #203): the image runs as user 65532 (the node agent stays root), the replication receiver has its own ServiceAccount, and receiver TLS stays off by default (turning it on needs cert-manager and a trusted CA on the source cluster). 9. The default image tag is v plus the chart appVersion, not latest. 10. The replication receiver memory limit is raised from 512Mi to 1Gi (replicationReceiver.resources.limits.memory). If you set your own value, check that it is at least 512Mi. The receiver now forces data out every 32 MiB for VM disks and plain files (PRs #219, #226). 11. Failover: apply the new SubVolume CRD (config/crd) before kubectl failover execute --rewind-to. The dry run now needs --kubeconfig because it reads the pool for the mount options. PVs it makes now carry sec=sys, and its PVCs bind only to the PV it made (PR #218). 12. Migrating a claim (kubectl migrate, console page) now runs as the namespace's user with the cluster's openshift/tools image. Owners are not kept and files unreadable to that user are not copied (PR #207; KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md). 13. Snapshot records of failed snapshots (not ready, older than 2 minutes, no VolumeSnapshotContent) are removed by the controller, including old leftovers (PR #204).

Fixes in this release: instant VM snapshot of a disk not owned by user 107 is refused and leaves the chain clean (#191, PR #194); replication and backup status follow the Jobs within seconds (#192, PR #197); the restore page no longer spins without the right to read VolumeSnapshotContents (#186, PR #188); a VM disk copy no longer sticks when its apply Job expires (#160, PR #161); kubectl backup cos-list works (PR #183).

Also fixed: receiver damaged upload record and Failed Jobs with in-place restarts (#213, PR #219); failover rewind path rule, mount options and StorageClass (#209 to #211, PR #218); plain-file receiver memory (#225, PR #226); #214 and #215 verified fixed by #161 and #197 (tests in PR #217).

Not in this release: auto-expand making a share inside the volume request (#222), the console restore banner (#224), failback (no command, untested), and file-level restore from a backup (issue #92). Parts 1 and 2 (the browse helper and the BackupBrowse resource with its session controller) are in the code, but nothing creates a BackupBrowse, so users see no change.

docs.title: Upgrading to v0.13.2 (from v0.13.1)
docs.text:
Fixes: Receiver Helm template ServiceAccount, ReplicationPolicy CRD validation, sync-client Job image selection, receiver path-doubling bug, scheduling fairness for parallel syncs.

CRD changes (additive): - ReplicationPolicy.spec.destinationNFSServer is now optional at the OpenAPI level (was incorrectly required, blocking driver-to-driver mode) - New field: ReplicationPolicy.spec.destinationCACertSecretRef — references a Secret containing a ca.crt key for verifying the receiver's TLS certificate (required for self-signed certs)

Action required: 1. Apply updated CRDs: kubectl apply -f config/crd/ 2. Upgrade controller — now passes --driver-image to receiver-mode sync-client Jobs automatically 3. If using driver-to-driver mode with TLS: create a Secret with the receiver's CA cert and set destinationCACertSecretRef on the ReplicationPolicy

New features: - Receiver TLS support — native HTTPS on the replication receiver via cert-manager. Enable with replicationReceiver.tls.enabled=true in Helm values. Creates a self-signed Issuer and Certificate automatically. OpenShift Route switches to passthrough TLS termination - --driver-image CLI flag and Helm wiring for receiver-mode sync-client Jobs - New CLI flags: --receiver-tls-cert-file, --receiver-tls-key-file (receiver), --ca-cert-file (sync-client) - Annotation-based pause/resume: storage.ibmcloud.io/paused=true on a ReplicationPolicy pauses replication; removing it resumes - Scheduling fairness: SubVolumes sorted by last-sync-time (oldest first) to prevent starvation under maxParallelSyncs limits - BytesWritten tracking: sync-client Jobs report bytes transferred via termination log; recorded in SubVolumeReplicationStatus.bytesSynced

Bug fixes: - Receiver path-doubling: when subPath already included the basePath prefix (e.g., /pvcs/pvc-xxx), the receiver would double it (e.g., /data/pvcs/pvcs/pvc-xxx). Now strips the prefix automatically - Sync-client Jobs now mount the CA cert Secret when destinationCACertSecretRef is set, enabling TLS verification for self-signed receiver certificates

docs.title: Upgrading to v0.13.1 (from v0.13.0)
docs.text:
Fixes: Console plugin table rows not rendering in tabbed layout.

No CRD changes. No RBAC changes. No data migration required.

Action required: 1. Upgrade controller — metrics now register with controller-runtime registry (fixes scraping when using Prometheus Operator) 2. Update image references from icr.io to de.icr.io (Frankfurt regional registry) if using explicit image tags

Console plugin changes: - Replaced VirtualizedTable with PatternFly composable Table in all 5 list pages - Added client-side column sorting on all list pages

docs.title: Upgrading to v0.13.0 (from v0.12.0)
docs.text:
New features: Console plugin tabbed navigation, CDI DataSource creation for InstanceTypes catalog, monitoring tab with Prometheus charts.

No CRD changes. No RBAC changes. No data migration required.

Action required: 1. Upgrade controller — golden image syncer now creates DataSource CRs in openshift-virtualization-os-images for InstanceTypes catalog visibility 2. If using the console plugin, the UI now uses a single tabbed interface instead of 7 sidebar items

Console plugin changes (if enabled): - Single "IBM VPC File Pools" sidebar entry with tabbed interface (Overview, Pools, SubVolumes, Snapshots, Group Snapshots, Replication, Monitoring) - New Monitoring tab with time-series charts and stat cards - IOPS column in pool table - Create buttons now route to custom form wizards instead of YAML editor

docs.title: Upgrading to v0.12.0 (from v0.11.0)
docs.text:
New feature: OpenShift Console dynamic plugin for visual pool management.

No CRD changes. No RBAC changes. No data migration required.

Console plugin is opt-in. The plugin is disabled by default (consolePlugin.enabled: false). To enable:

helm upgrade ibm-vpc-file-pool-csi charts/ibm-vpc-file-pool-csi/ \
  --namespace kube-system \
  --set consolePlugin.enabled=true \
  --reuse-values

After upgrade, register the plugin with the console:

# Adds this plugin to the list and keeps the other plugins enabled.
# (A merge patch with a "plugins" list would replace the whole list.)
oc patch console.operator.openshift.io cluster --type=json \
  -p '[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/plugins/-","value":"ibm-vpc-file-pool-csi"}]'

Requires OpenShift 4.14+ with the ConsolePlugin v1 API. Non-OpenShift clusters can skip this — no impact on existing functionality.

docs.title: Upgrading to v0.11.0 (from v0.10.0)
docs.text:
New features: Golden image syncer, mount target recovery, selectShare IP guard.

CRD changes (additive): - FileSharePool.spec.goldenImages — new optional field for golden image syncer config - FileSharePool.status.goldenImages — new status field for per-image sync state

RBAC changes: ClusterRole extended with cdi.kubevirt.io (dataimportcrons, datasources), batch/jobs, and template.openshift.io/templates. Apply updated RBAC before upgrading.

Action required: 1. Apply updated CRDs: kubectl apply -f config/crd/ 2. Apply updated RBAC: kubectl apply -f config/rbac/ 3. Upgrade controller — the new mount target recovery and IP guard activate automatically 4. (Optional) Configure spec.goldenImages on FileSharePool CRs if using KubeVirt

No data migration required. Shares with missing mount targets are automatically recovered or drained.

docs.title: Upgrading to v0.10.0 (from v0.9.0)
docs.text:
New features: NFS sec=sys default mount option, CDI StorageProfile auto-patching.

Action required: 1. Upgrade controller and node DaemonSet 2. Existing NFS mounts continue with their current sec= negotiation. New mounts get sec=sys automatically. 3. To apply sec=sys to existing mounts, restart the node DaemonSet pods (rolling restart happens automatically during upgrade)

KubeVirt users: This upgrade fixes the "chown operation not permitted" issue. After upgrade, restart affected VMs.

docs.title: Upgrading to v0.9.0 (from v0.8.0)
docs.text:
Critical fix: NFS mount used server root instead of share export path.

CRD changes (additive): - PoolShareStatus.ExportPath — new field for NFS export path - ZoneMountTarget.ExportPath — new field - SubVolumeSpec.ShareExportPath — new field

Action required: 1. Apply updated CRDs: kubectl apply -f config/crd/ 2. Upgrade controller — existing shares without export paths are automatically backfilled during the reconciler's health check 3. Upgrade node DaemonSet — new mounts use the correct export path

No manual data migration required. The health check backfill handles existing shares.

docs.title: Upgrading to v0.8.0 (from v0.7.0)
docs.text:
Fixes: Hardcoded staging path, mount flags override, resource requests/limits, probes, webhook cert permissions.

Action required: 1. Apply updated CRDs 2. Upgrade controller — now includes --kubelet-dir flag wired through Helm 3. Upgrade node DaemonSet — gains resource limits, probes, and readiness checks

ROKS and ROVS users: Verify node.kubeletDir is set to /var/data/kubelet in your Helm values. The controller's staging path now respects this setting.

docs.title: Upgrading to v0.7.0 (from v0.6.0)
docs.text:
New feature: Automatic StorageClass creation.

RBAC changes: Controller ClusterRole needs create verb for storageclasses.

Action required: 1. Apply updated RBAC: kubectl apply -f config/rbac/ 2. Apply updated CRDs 3. Upgrade controller — auto-creates StorageClasses for existing pools

Note: If you already have manually created StorageClasses, they are not overwritten. To opt out of auto-creation, annotate the pool: 

kubectl annotate filesharepool <pool-name> storage.ibmcloud.io/skip-storageclass="true"

docs.title: Upgrading to v0.6.0 (from v0.5.0)
docs.text:
New features: Validating admission webhooks, lifecycle hooks, incremental rsync.

Prerequisites: - cert-manager v1.12+ must be installed (for webhook TLS certificates). ROVS has no cert-manager; on ROKS and ROVS you can set webhook.certProvider=openshift instead (see INSTALL.md — Webhook Certificates)

CRD changes (additive): - ReplicationPolicy.spec.preSyncHooks / postSyncHooks — new hook fields - ReplicationPolicy.spec.incrementalSync — new field (default true) - VolumeGroupSnapshot.spec.preSnapshotHooks / postSnapshotHooks — new hook fields - New CRD types: Hook, ExecHookSpec, HTTPHookSpec, HookResult

Action required: 1. Install cert-manager if not already present: kubectl apply -f https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/releases/latest/download/cert-manager.yaml 2. Apply updated CRDs: kubectl apply -f config/crd/ 3. Apply webhook configurations: kubectl apply -f config/webhook/ 4. Upgrade controller

Known issue fixed: VPC auto-discovery silent failure — if you experienced pools without mount targets, this version fixes it by using kubernetes.Clientset for pre-start ConfigMap reads.

docs.title: Upgrading to v0.5.0 (from v0.4.0)
docs.text:
New feature: Cross-region disaster recovery (ReplicationPolicy CRD).

CRD changes (additive): - New CRD: ReplicationPolicy

Action required: 1. Apply new CRD: kubectl apply -f config/crd/ 2. Upgrade controller 3. (Optional) Create ReplicationPolicy CRs for DR — see CROSS-REGION-DR.md

docs.title: Upgrading to v0.4.0 (from v0.3.0)
docs.text:
New features: Volume snapshots, volume cloning, volume group snapshots, share draining, migration CLI.

CRD changes (additive): - New CRD: Snapshot - New CRD: VolumeGroupSnapshot - SubVolume gains clone fields: sourceVolume, sourceShareID, cloneStatus, cloneProgress - FileSharePool.spec.drainShares — new field for graceful share draining

Prerequisites: - VolumeSnapshot CRDs must be installed (external-snapshotter): 

kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kubernetes-csi/external-snapshotter/master/client/config/crd/

Action required: 1. Install VolumeSnapshot CRDs (if not already present) 2. Apply updated CRDs: kubectl apply -f config/crd/ 3. Upgrade controller and node DaemonSet 4. (Optional) Create VolumeSnapshotClass for the pool driver

docs.title: Upgrading to v0.3.0 (from v0.2.0)
docs.text:
New features: Cross-zone accessor binding, idempotent CreateFileShare, nsenter mount wrapper.

CRD changes (additive): - FileSharePool.spec.accessorZones — new field for multi-zone mount targets - PoolShareStatus.mountTargets — new status field (ZoneMountTarget array)

Action required: 1. Apply updated CRDs: kubectl apply -f config/crd/ 2. Upgrade controller and node DaemonSet 3. Node DaemonSet now requires hostPID: true for the nsenter mount wrapper — verify your DaemonSet spec includes this

docs.title: Upgrading to v0.2.0 (from v0.1.0)
docs.text:
New features: Share tiering, per-PVC usage reporting, Prometheus metrics, auto-discovery.

CRD changes (additive): - FileSharePool.spec.tiers — new optional field for tiered storage - Various status fields for metrics

Action required: 1. Apply updated CRDs: kubectl apply -f config/crd/ 2. Upgrade controller — metrics endpoint becomes available on :8080/metrics 3. (Optional) Configure Prometheus scraping — see MONITORING.md 4. (Optional) Configure tiered storage if needed

docs.title: Fresh Install: v0.1.0
docs.text: Initial release. See INSTALL.md for first-time installation.

docs.title: Helm Rollback
docs.text:
# List revision history
helm history ibm-vpc-file-pool-csi -n kube-system

# Rollback to previous revision
helm rollback ibm-vpc-file-pool-csi <revision-number> -n kube-system

docs.title: Manual Rollback
docs.text:
# Reapply the previous version's manifests
kubectl apply -f config/controller/  # previous version
kubectl apply -f config/node/        # previous version

docs.title: CRD Rollback Caveats
docs.text:
Helm does not roll back CRDs. If the upgrade added new CRD fields, those fields remain in the CRD schema after rollback. This is generally safe because:

  • New fields are optional with defaults
  • The older controller version ignores unknown fields
  • Existing CR data is preserved

If you need to roll back a CRD, apply the previous version's CRD manifests manually:

kubectl apply -f config/crd/  # from the previous version's checkout

Warning: Rolling back CRDs that removed fields can cause data loss in those fields. Always back up CRs before rollback (see pre-flight checklist).

docs.title: Post-Upgrade Verification
docs.text:
Run this checklist after every upgrade:

# 1. Verify all pods are running
kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l app.kubernetes.io/name=ibm-vpc-file-pool-csi,app.kubernetes.io/component=controller
kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l app.kubernetes.io/name=ibm-vpc-file-pool-csi,app.kubernetes.io/component=node

# 2. Verify all pools are Ready
kubectl get filesharepools

# 3. Verify CSI driver is registered
kubectl get csidriver vpc-file-pool.csi.ibm.io

# 4. Test PVC creation (create a test PVC and verify it binds)
kubectl apply -f - <<'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: upgrade-test-pvc
  namespace: default
spec:
  accessModes: [ReadWriteMany]
  storageClassName: ibm-vpc-file-pool
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
EOF
kubectl get pvc upgrade-test-pvc -w  # Should bind within seconds

# 5. Verify metrics endpoint (if applicable)
kubectl port-forward -n kube-system svc/ibm-vpc-file-pool-csi-metrics 8080:8080 &
curl -s http://localhost:8080/metrics | grep vpc_file_pool | head -5
kill %1

# 6. Clean up test PVC
kubectl delete pvc upgrade-test-pvc

# 7. Check controller logs for errors
kubectl logs -n kube-system -l app.kubernetes.io/name=ibm-vpc-file-pool-csi,app.kubernetes.io/component=controller -c csi-controller --tail=50 | grep -i "error\|fail"

docs.title: Downtime Expectations
docs.text:
Component Downtime Impact Controller ~30 seconds Leader election gap. New PVC creation pauses during the gap. Existing mounted PVCs are unaffected. Node DaemonSet Rolling update, ~60s per node No mount disruption for existing pods. New NodePublishVolume calls queue until the new pod is ready. CRD apply None CRD updates are live. Existing CRs continue to work. Webhook update ~10 seconds CRD creation/update requests may briefly fail validation. Retry resolves this.

Zero-downtime for existing workloads. Pods with mounted PVCs are not affected by controller or node agent upgrades — NFS mounts are kernel-level and persist independently of the CSI driver pods.

docs.title: User Guide — IBM VPC File Pool CSI Driver
docs.text: For the meaning of project words such as pool, share, SubVolume and snapshot, see CONTEXT.md.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
The IBM VPC File Pool CSI Driver changes the relationship between PVCs and VPC file shares. Instead of one PVC creating one share, many PVCs share a common pool of large file shares. Each PVC gets its own subdirectory on a share.

This means PVCs provision in under a second (a mkdir vs. a 30-90 second API call), you use a fraction of your 300-share quota, and small PVCs don't each waste a 10 GB minimum allocation.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
Get a PVC running in 4 steps:

# 1. Create a pool (if one doesn't exist yet)
kubectl apply -f examples/basic/pool.yaml
kubectl get filesharepools -w          # Wait for Phase: Ready (~60 seconds)

# 2. Create a StorageClass
kubectl apply -f examples/basic/storageclass.yaml

# 3. Create a PVC
kubectl apply -f examples/basic/pvc.yaml
kubectl get pvc my-app-data            # Should be Bound within seconds

# 4. Use the PVC in a pod
kubectl apply -f examples/basic/pod.yaml
kubectl logs my-app-pod                # Should print "Hello from pool CSI"

See examples/ for more patterns: multi-zone, StatefulSet, shared RWX, tiered performance, custom permissions, and data retention.

docs.title: FileSharePool
docs.text:
A FileSharePool is a cluster-scoped custom resource that defines a pool of VPC file shares. It specifies the zone, storage profile, share size, and capacity management rules. The driver's controller watches these resources and ensures enough VPC file shares exist to serve PVC requests.

You can have multiple pools for different use cases — for example a high-IOPS pool for databases and a standard pool for application configs.

docs.title: SubVolume
docs.text: A SubVolume is a cluster-scoped custom resource that tracks a single PVC's allocation. It records which share the PVC's subdirectory lives on, the mount target IP, the subdirectory path, and the requested capacity. SubVolumes are created automatically when you create a PVC and deleted when the PVC is deleted.

docs.title: StorageClass
docs.text: A standard Kubernetes StorageClass that references a pool by name. You create PVCs against this StorageClass just like any other CSI driver.

docs.title: Creating a Pool
docs.text:
apiVersion: storage.ibmcloud.io/v1alpha1
kind: FileSharePool
metadata:
  name: general-purpose
spec:
  zone: us-south-1
  profile: dp2
  shareSizeGB: 2000
  maxShares: 10
  initialShares: 1
  autoExpand: true
  expandThresholdPercent: 80
  allocationStrategy: spread
  defaultPermissions: "0755"
  defaultUID: 1000    # UID owner for subdirectories
  defaultGID: 1000    # GID owner for subdirectories
  # Authentication is handled globally via secret-common-lib (no secretRef needed)
  mountOptions:
    - nfsvers=4.1
    - soft
    - timeo=600
    - retrans=3

kubectl apply -f pool.yaml

Wait for the pool phase to become Ready:

kubectl get filesharepools

NAME              ZONE         PROFILE  SHARES  CAPACITY  ALLOCATED  PVCS  PHASE
general-purpose   us-south-1   dp2      1       2000      0          0     Ready

docs.title: Pool Sizing Guidance
docs.text:
Workload Type Suggested Profile Share Size IOPS Strategy General workloads (configs, logs, small apps) dp2 1000-2000 GB 1,000 spread Databases, analytics dp2 2000-4000 GB set spec.iops (higher) spread CI/CD ephemeral volumes dp2 500-1000 GB unset (100) binpack Shared team storage dp2 4000+ GB 1,000 or more spread

Rules of thumb: - shareSizeGB should be large enough to hold 50-200 PVCs without needing a new share. If most PVCs are 1-5 GB, a 1 TB share gives you 200-1000 PVCs per share. - maxShares controls your maximum VPC file share quota usage per pool. With 300 shares per account, budget across your pools and the stock IBM CSI driver. - expandThresholdPercent at 80% means a new share is created when 80% of the pool's total capacity is allocated. This gives a buffer so PVCs don't fail while the new share is being created (30-90 seconds). - allocationStrategy: spread distributes PVCs evenly across shares (better fault isolation); binpack fills shares before starting new ones (fewer shares used, but higher blast radius if one fails).

docs.title: Viewing Pool Status
docs.text:
# Summary
kubectl get filesharepools

# Detailed status with per-share breakdown
kubectl get filesharepool general-purpose -o yaml

The status section shows each share's ID, mount target IP, total/allocated capacity, PVC count, and health state.

docs.title: Multi-Zone Clusters
docs.text:
Each pool lives in one zone (spec.zone), and all its shares are created in that zone. In security group access mode, each share has one mount target in that zone, and pods in every zone can mount it. A single pool therefore serves a cluster that spans zones. IBM documents cross-zone mounting for security group mode; this project has not yet tested it on a multi-zone cluster. The accessorZones field is optional and not used.

Cross-zone traffic adds latency. To keep data and traffic in one zone, create one pool per zone:

# pool-south-1.yaml
apiVersion: storage.ibmcloud.io/v1alpha1
kind: FileSharePool
metadata:
  name: general-us-south-1
spec:
  zone: us-south-1
  # ...rest of spec
---
# pool-south-2.yaml
apiVersion: storage.ibmcloud.io/v1alpha1
kind: FileSharePool
metadata:
  name: general-us-south-2
spec:
  zone: us-south-2
  # ...rest of spec

Then create a StorageClass per zone, or a single StorageClass with volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer and topology awareness (the driver will pick the pool matching the pod's zone).

docs.title: Expanding a Pool Manually
docs.text:
If autoExpand is false or you want to proactively add capacity:

# Option 1: Increase maxShares and let the reconciler add shares as needed
kubectl patch filesharepool general-purpose --type merge -p '{"spec":{"maxShares":15}}'

# Option 2: Lower expandThresholdPercent so the reconciler adds a share sooner
# (Changing shareSizeGB only sets the size of shares created afterwards;
#  existing shares keep their size.)

docs.title: Draining a Share
docs.text:
If you need to take a share out of rotation (e.g., for maintenance or migration), the pool manager supports a draining state where no new PVCs are allocated to that share but existing PVCs continue to work. This is managed automatically when the VPC API reports a share as degraded.

To drain a share by hand, add its ID to spec.drainShares on the pool. See DAY2-OPERATIONS.md.

docs.title: Default StorageClass
docs.text:
The installation creates a default StorageClass:

apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: ibm-vpc-file-pool
provisioner: vpc-file-pool.csi.ibm.io
parameters:
  pool: general-purpose
reclaimPolicy: Delete
volumeBindingMode: Immediate
allowVolumeExpansion: true
mountOptions:
  - nfsvers=4.1
  - soft
  - timeo=600
  - retrans=3

docs.title: Custom StorageClasses
docs.text:
Create StorageClasses for different use cases:

# High-security: specific UID/GID, restricted permissions
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: ibm-vpc-file-pool-secure
provisioner: vpc-file-pool.csi.ibm.io
parameters:
  pool: general-purpose
  uid: "65534"
  gid: "65534"
  permissions: "0700"
reclaimPolicy: Delete
volumeBindingMode: Immediate
allowVolumeExpansion: true
mountOptions:
  - nfsvers=4.1
  - soft
  - timeo=600
  - retrans=3
---
# Retain data after PVC deletion
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: ibm-vpc-file-pool-retain
provisioner: vpc-file-pool.csi.ibm.io
parameters:
  pool: general-purpose
reclaimPolicy: Retain
volumeBindingMode: Immediate
allowVolumeExpansion: true
mountOptions:
  - nfsvers=4.1
  - soft
  - timeo=600
  - retrans=3

docs.title: StorageClass Parameters Reference
docs.text: Parameter Required Default Description pool Yes — Name of the FileSharePool CR to allocate from uid No Pool's defaultUID Unix UID owner for the subdirectory gid No Pool's defaultGID Unix GID owner for the subdirectory permissions No Pool's defaultPermissions Unix permissions (e.g., "0755")

docs.title: Creating a PVC
docs.text:
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: my-app-data
  namespace: default
spec:
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteMany        # NFS supports RWX natively
  storageClassName: ibm-vpc-file-pool
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 5Gi

kubectl apply -f pvc.yaml

# PVC should bind within seconds
kubectl get pvc my-app-data

docs.title: Access Modes
docs.text:
Since the underlying storage is NFS, all access modes work:

Mode Supported Description ReadWriteOnce (RWO) Yes Single node read-write ReadOnlyMany (ROX) Yes Multiple nodes read-only ReadWriteMany (RWX) Yes Multiple nodes read-write ReadWriteOncePod (RWOP) Yes Single pod read-write (K8s 1.29+)

RWX is the natural fit for this driver since NFS is inherently multi-reader/writer. Use it for shared storage across replicas, batch jobs, and cross-pod data.

docs.title: Using a PVC in a Pod
docs.text:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: my-app
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: my-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: my-app
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: my-app:latest
          volumeMounts:
            - name: data
              mountPath: /data
          securityContext:
            runAsUser: 1000        # Should match StorageClass uid
            runAsGroup: 1000       # Should match StorageClass gid
      volumes:
        - name: data
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: my-app-data

docs.title: Expanding a PVC
docs.text:
# Edit the PVC to request more storage
kubectl patch pvc my-app-data -p '{"spec":{"resources":{"requests":{"storage":"20Gi"}}}}'

# Check the new size
kubectl get pvc my-app-data

Expansion is nearly instant — the driver updates the allocation tracking in the SubVolume CR. No VPC API call is needed unless the share itself needs to grow.

Note: You can only expand, not shrink. This is a Kubernetes-wide constraint on PVCs.

docs.title: Deleting a PVC
docs.text:
kubectl delete pvc my-app-data

What happens depends on the StorageClass's reclaim policy:

  • Delete (default): The subdirectory and all its contents are removed from the share. The SubVolume CR is deleted. Capacity is freed in the pool.
  • Retain (reclaimPolicy: Retain on the StorageClass): Kubernetes keeps the PersistentVolume and never asks the driver to delete it. The SubVolume CR and the subdirectory stay too. Clean them up by hand when the data is no longer needed.

docs.title: Viewing SubVolumes
docs.text:
# All subvolumes
kubectl get subvolumes

# Detailed view
kubectl get subvolumes -o wide

# Filter by pool
kubectl get subvolumes -l storage.ibmcloud.io/pool=general-purpose

# Filter by share
kubectl get subvolumes -l storage.ibmcloud.io/share-id=r006-xxxx

# Detailed status for a specific subvolume
kubectl get subvolume pvc-abc123 -o yaml

docs.title: Create a VM with its boot disk on a pool
docs.text:
Use the standard OpenShift Virtualization catalog. The driver needs no special image setup.

  1. In the OpenShift console, open Virtualization and then the Catalog.
  2. Pick a catalog image, such as CentOS Stream 9 or RHEL 9, and an instance type.
  3. For the boot disk, choose the pool's StorageClass.
  4. Create the VM.

CDI copies the catalog image onto the pool, then the VM starts. Part 15 of the tutorial series walks through it. On rovslab, a RHEL 9 VM had its guest agent about 103 seconds after it was created.

The controller keeps the memory limit of CDI's copy pods at least 8Gi. Without it, the copy pod is killed for lack of memory. On ROVS, IBM manages the virtualization settings; see KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md. If a copy fails, see TROUBLESHOOTING.md.

Golden images (spec.goldenImages) are hidden and kept for possible later use. See GOLDEN-IMAGE-WORKFLOW.md.

docs.title: Creating a Snapshot
docs.text:
Create a VolumeSnapshot referencing an existing PVC to capture a point-in-time copy of the data:

apiVersion: snapshot.storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: VolumeSnapshot
metadata:
  name: my-app-snapshot
  namespace: default
spec:
  volumeSnapshotClassName: ibm-vpc-file-pool
  source:
    persistentVolumeClaimName: my-app-data

kubectl apply -f snapshot.yaml

# Check snapshot status
kubectl get volumesnapshot my-app-snapshot

For a plain volume, the snapshot is a directory copy under /pvcs/.snapshots/ on the same share, and its creation time is proportional to data size. For a VM disk, it is a QEMU copy or an instant snapshot (see CONTEXT.md).

docs.title: Restoring from a Snapshot
docs.text:
Create a new PVC with dataSource referencing the snapshot:

apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: my-app-restored
  namespace: default
spec:
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteMany
  storageClassName: ibm-vpc-file-pool
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 5Gi
  dataSource:
    name: my-app-snapshot
    kind: VolumeSnapshot
    apiGroup: snapshot.storage.k8s.io

docs.title: Deleting a Snapshot
docs.text:
kubectl delete volumesnapshot my-app-snapshot

This removes the snapshot directory and frees capacity on the share.

docs.title: Cloning a PVC
docs.text:
Create a new PVC with dataSource referencing an existing PVC:

apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: my-app-clone
  namespace: default
spec:
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteMany
  storageClassName: ibm-vpc-file-pool
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 5Gi          # Must be >= source PVC size
  dataSource:
    kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
    name: my-app-data        # Source PVC in the same namespace

kubectl apply -f clone-pvc.yaml

# Check clone status
kubectl get subvolumes -l storage.ibmcloud.io/clone-source

Every clone is asynchronous, whatever the volume size. The PVC binds immediately but pods wait in ContainerCreating until the background copy completes. Monitor progress via the SubVolume CR's cloneStatus field.

docs.title: Clone Consistency
docs.text:
• Best practice: Scale down the application or pause writes before cloning for full consistency.
  • If the source is being actively written to, each file is individually consistent (NFS close-to-open), but cross-file relationships are not guaranteed.
  • Do not clone running VM disk images — the clone will be corrupt.

docs.title: Volume Group Snapshots
docs.text:
Not active (issue #100). The driver does not act on VolumeGroupSnapshot records. The hooks never run and there is no plan to turn them on. The examples below do nothing. A running VM with several disks does not need group snapshots: its snapshots show one moment already (see KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md).

Group snapshots coordinate the snapshot of multiple related PVCs in a single operation.

docs.title: Creating a Group Snapshot
docs.text:
apiVersion: storage.ibmcloud.io/v1alpha1
kind: VolumeGroupSnapshot
metadata:
  name: myapp-group-snap
spec:
  poolName: general-purpose
  sourcePVCs:
    - pvcName: myapp-data
      pvcNamespace: default
    - pvcName: myapp-wal
      pvcNamespace: default
    - pvcName: myapp-config
      pvcNamespace: default
  failurePolicy: Abort          # Abort or Continue

kubectl apply -f group-snapshot.yaml

# Check group snapshot status
kubectl get volumegroupsnapshots myapp-group-snap

docs.title: Group Snapshot Consistency
docs.text:
Without quiesce hooks (current implementation), group snapshots provide best-effort coordinated consistency — SubVolumes are copied sequentially with an inconsistency window equal to the total copy duration.

For workloads requiring cross-PVC consistency, scale down the application before taking the group snapshot.

docs.title: Deleting a Group Snapshot
docs.text:
kubectl delete volumegroupsnapshot myapp-group-snap

This deletes all member snapshots and frees the associated capacity.

docs.title: Coexistence with the Stock IBM CSI Driver
docs.text:
This driver runs alongside the stock ibm-vpc-file-csi-driver without conflict. They use different provisioner names:

Driver Provisioner Name Stock IBM File CSI vpc.file.csi.ibm.io Pool File CSI (this driver) vpc-file-pool.csi.ibm.io

Use the stock driver for workloads that need a dedicated share with isolated IOPS (e.g., a high-traffic database). Use the pool driver for everything else — application configs, shared data, CI/CD volumes, log storage, and any workload where fast provisioning and efficient quota usage matter more than per-PVC IOPS isolation.

Both StorageClasses can exist at the same time. Pods pick which driver to use by referencing the appropriate StorageClass.

docs.title: Prometheus Metrics
docs.text:
The controller exposes metrics on :8080/metrics. Scrape this endpoint with Prometheus or use the ServiceMonitor if your cluster runs the Prometheus Operator.

Key metrics:

Metric Type Description vpc_file_pool_capacity_gb Gauge Total capacity across all shares in a pool vpc_file_pool_allocated_gb Gauge Total allocated (requested) capacity in a pool vpc_file_pool_pvc_count Gauge Number of active PVCs in a pool vpc_file_pool_share_count Gauge Number of VPC file shares in a pool vpc_file_pool_allocations_total Counter Cumulative PVC allocations (by pool; status success, error, deallocate_success or deallocate_error) vpc_file_pool_allocation_duration_seconds Histogram Time to allocate a PVC (should be <1s in steady state) vpc_file_pool_api_calls_total Counter VPC API calls (by operation, success/error) vpc_file_pool_api_call_duration_seconds Histogram VPC API call duration

docs.title: Recommended Alerts
docs.text:
# Pool near capacity
- alert: FileSharePoolNearCapacity
  expr: vpc_file_pool_allocated_gb / vpc_file_pool_capacity_gb > 0.9
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: warning
  annotations:
    summary: "File share pool {{ $labels.pool }} is over 90% allocated"

# Pool at max shares
- alert: FileSharePoolAtMaxShares
  expr: vpc_file_pool_share_count >= on(pool) group_left max by(pool) (vpc_file_pool_max_shares)
  for: 1m
  labels:
    severity: critical
  annotations:
    summary: "File share pool {{ $labels.pool }} has reached max shares and cannot auto-expand"

# PVC allocation failures
- alert: FileSharePoolAllocationFailures
  expr: rate(vpc_file_pool_allocations_total{status="error"}[5m]) > 0
  for: 2m
  labels:
    severity: warning
  annotations:
    summary: "PVC allocations failing in pool {{ $labels.pool }}"

# VPC API errors
- alert: VPCAPIErrors
  expr: rate(vpc_file_pool_api_calls_total{status="error"}[5m]) > 0.1
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: warning
  annotations:
    summary: "VPC API errors detected for {{ $labels.operation }}"

docs.title: Checking Pool Health
docs.text:
# Quick health check
kubectl get filesharepools

# If a pool shows "Degraded", check which share is unhealthy
kubectl get filesharepool <pool-name> -o jsonpath='{range .status.shares[*]}{.shareID}{"\t"}{.state}{"\n"}{end}'

# Check controller logs for reconciliation errors
kubectl logs -n kube-system -l app.kubernetes.io/name=ibm-vpc-file-pool-csi,app.kubernetes.io/component=controller -c csi-controller --tail=50

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Here are the three most common issues. For the full troubleshooting guide (pool issues, VPC API errors, mount debugging, metrics, logging), see TROUBLESHOOTING.md.

docs.title: PVC Pending: "pool not found"
docs.text:
The pool parameter in the StorageClass doesn't match any FileSharePool CR name. Verify with: 

kubectl get filesharepools
kubectl get storageclass <sc-name> -o jsonpath='{.parameters.pool}'

docs.title: NFS mount failed
docs.text: TCP port 2049 is blocked between worker nodes and NFS mount targets. Check security group rules. See TROUBLESHOOTING.md — Mount Issues for detailed steps.

docs.title: Permission denied
docs.text: UID/GID mismatch between the pod's securityContext and the StorageClass's uid/gid parameters. See TROUBLESHOOTING.md — Permission denied for details.

docs.title: Frequently Asked Questions
docs.text:
Q: Can I use this with OpenShift? Yes. The driver is fully compatible with ROKS and ROVS (Red Hat OpenShift on IBM Cloud). On OpenShift, the node agent requires the privileged SCC, which is standard for all CSI node agents. The chart's ClusterRole lets the node agent use the privileged SCC. If your cluster does not grant it, bind the SCC to the node agent's ServiceAccount with oc adm policy add-scc-to-user privileged -z <node service account> -n kube-system.

Q: What happens if a VPC file share goes down? All PVCs on that share will experience I/O errors until the share recovers. IBM VPC File Storage has 99.999% availability with HA-paired nodes, so this is extremely rare. The pool manager will detect the degraded state and stop allocating new PVCs to that share. Existing PVCs recover automatically when the share comes back.

Q: Can I migrate existing PVCs from the stock IBM CSI driver to this driver? Not in-place — Kubernetes doesn't support changing a PV's CSI driver. You would need to create a new PVC with the pool StorageClass, copy the data (e.g., with rsync in a pod that mounts both PVCs), then switch your application to the new PVC. The kubectl migrate plugin does this for you. See TUTORIAL-08-MIGRATION-AND-CONSOLE.md.

Q: Is there per-PVC quota enforcement? Currently, quotas are advisory (soft enforcement). The driver tracks allocated vs. requested capacity in SubVolume CRs, and the metrics/alerts system will warn you when a PVC exceeds its allocation. Hard per-subdirectory quotas depend on NFS server-side project quota support, which IBM VPC File Storage does not currently expose. If hard quotas are critical for your use case, use the stock IBM CSI driver for those specific workloads.

Q: How many PVCs can I have per share? There's no hard limit in the driver. The practical limits are the share's total capacity and the NFS server's ability to handle concurrent connections. In testing, hundreds of PVCs per share work well. If you're running thousands, monitor NFS connection counts and consider spreading across more shares (use the spread allocation strategy).

Q: Can I use this across multiple availability zones? Yes. One pool serves pods in every zone through the share's single mount target, which sits in the pool's zone. This has not yet been tested on a multi-zone cluster. Cross-zone traffic adds latency. To avoid it, create one pool per zone with separate StorageClasses. See Multi-Zone Clusters.

Q: Does this work with IBM Cloud Satellite? This driver targets IBM Cloud VPC infrastructure specifically (it uses the VPC API to create file shares). For Satellite locations with their own storage backends, the community csi-driver-nfs may be more appropriate since it works with any existing NFS server.
